TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The global treatment line at the paper mill consists of anaerobic digestion, aerobic digestion, a sedimentation process, and rejecting the water to the river. In order to reuse the process water, a pilot test was completed where a filtration technology and a softening technology were added downstream of the global treatment line. The filtration technology used is a flexible fiber filter module called the 3FM process. The softening technology used was the Multiflo softening system.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: lime, carbonate ion, metallic salts, polymer (added to the Multiflo system)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 3FM process: head-loss increases during the filtration cycle and the filtration capacity is recovered by periodic backwashing with a small amount of influent waste water and scouring air. Flow rate = 2 m3/hr and periodic backwashes were initially programmed every 4 hours. Multiflow Softening System: flow rate = 125 L/hr with a total residence time of 30 minutes.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Rinse water is treated with chemical precipitation, then passed through ultra-filtration membranes and reverse osmosis.  Most water is then reused.  Waste is thickened with a centrifuge and dewatered with a plate/frame press.

The effluent from the inorganic wastewater treatment process (lime addition for the removal of fluoride and phosphate) was used as the influent of this pilot test. The influent was fed to the seed activation tank and completely mixed with the activated calcite seeds and a sodium carbonate solution (soda ash) to precipitate calcium in the form of calcite (a calcium carbonate mineral). The calcite seed activation was achieved using the controlled hydrodynamic cavitation (CHC) unit. The wastewater then flowed into the clarifier equipped with a scrapper, where the settled calcite slurry was then returned to the seed activation tank for activation of the calcites.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium carbonate (soda ash) dose rate: 940 mg/L (based on influent flowrate)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: CHC unit flowrate: 14,440 gpd (54.5 m3/d), Calcium carbonate storage tank temperature: 90 – 102 degrees Fahrenheit

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The biological treatment system includes three reactors in series, each containing plastic rock-sized media for bacterial attachment. The system is a packed bed system with a high biomass quantity per unit volume. After water is pumped to the first reactor, it flows by gravity through the rest of the treatment and infiltration system.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Methanol
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design criteria included a flow rate of 10 gpm, a nitrate-nitrogen concentration of 6 g/L, and a sulfate concentration of 120 mg/L.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The biological treatment system includes methanol and phosphate addition and then three treatment cells in series. The first cell has denitrification with plastic media, the second and third cells are designed for sulfate reduction with rock media.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Methanol, phosphate
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design criteria included a flow rate of 50 gpm, a nitrate-nitrogen concentration of 33 g/L, a sulfate concentration of 800 mg/L, a 99-hour residence time, and a water temperature as low as 2 Degrees Celsius (during winter).

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Acid Mine Drainage (AMD) is treated in a set of four mixer-settler units. First, the AMD is mixed with an organic extractant solution that partitions the iron and sulfate ions to the extractant. After separation, clean water flows out of the system, while the extractant flows to metal and sulfate recovery stages. During the metal recovery stage, the extractant is mixed with sulfuric acid in a set of 2 to 3 metal cation recovery tanks, which forms an iron sulfate concentrate that is collected for reuse. During the sulfate recovery stage, the extractant is mixed with potassium carbonate in a series of mixer-settler tanks, which forms a potassium sulfate concentrate that is collected for sale or reuse. The extractant exits the last mixer-settler and is ready to contact a new stream of AMD feed water.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Unnamed organic extractant solution, sulfuric acid, and potassium carbonate.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: AMD and extractant are mixed with a residence time of 60 to 90 seconds.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system includes a holding tank, pre-filtration with bag filters followed by cartridges for solids removal, and two 60 cubic foot ion exchange (IX) tanks for metals removal. The IX system is modular with a commercial cation exchange resin. The pre-filters remove some suspended solids, but the remaining solids plug the IX tanks before the full chemical removal capacity of the resin can be utilized.
OANDM_COST: IX Tanks - $10,000/exchange

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The effluent is separated into three streams: chromium rinse, nickel rinse, and water treatment. Each stream has a dedicated flash vacuum distillation unit. The distillate is pretreated with granular activated carbon (GAC) and oil filtration media, and then polished with an ion exchange system with 1-5 megaohm resistivity. The recovered water is disinfected with UV light, treated with an ultrafilter, and reused as rinse water. The nickel and chromium are recovered by the two vacuum chamber units and returned to the plating baths.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Evaporation occurs in the vacuum at 100 to 140 degrees Fahrenheit. Chrome and nickel rinse waters are each treated with a dedicated 2,000 gpd unit. Process wastewaters are treated with a dedicated a 5,000 gpd unit.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: An undersized treatment system was upgraded and expanded with a Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (MBBR) system to meet increasing processing demand.  The MBBR uses polyethylene biofilm carrier elements on which bacterial cultures grow within the reactor tank to treat the water. Effluent from the biofilm systems flows via gravity directly to the downstream activated sludge system. The activated sludge aeration basins were upgraded from an outdated differ system to a medium bubble aeration to maintain dissolved oxygen levels in the mixed liquor suspended solids.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: MBBR reactor capacity is 180,000 gallons. The facility design capacity is 18,100 lbs of BOD5 per day. The design flow is 140,000 gpd effluent at 15,500 mg/L BOD5 and the MBBR process is capable of removing 11,600 lbs of BOD5 per day.

INDUSTRY: Canned and preserved fruits and vegetables processing
TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: After passing through a self-cleaning rotary screen that captures particles larger than 1mm (i.e., mustard seeds, bottle caps, and other solid waste), the wastewater is collected in a mechanically-mixed equalization (EQ) tank. The EQ tank receives process wastewater and rainwater run-off that must be collected as part of pre-treatment. When EQ tank reaches a volume of 25-30%, caustic soda is added to increase pH and wastewater begins transferring to the two-stage bioreactor. This transfer includes rationed doses of ammonia, phosphorous, and a defoaming agent depending on wastewater composition. The first bioreactor uses suspended biofilm carriers where bacteria provide a BOD roughing process that removes 50% to 70% of the BOD. The second bioreactor decreases BOD to within effluent parameters. Treated wastewater then flows by gravity to a dissolved air flotation (DAF) to clarify water before final transfer to the municipal wastewater treatment plant. A recirculation loop gives the facility the ability to reprocess water if additional treatment is necessary.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Caustic Soda, Ammonia, Phosphorous, Defoaming Agent
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: EQ tank capacity: 100,000 gallons; Bioreactor flow rate: 14gpm; Bioreactor capacity: 15,000 gallons per reactor

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system utilizes aluminosilicate (zeolite) filtration media to remove dissolved iron. This is followed by a two-stage ion exchange unit that uses in each stage a weak acid cation as a catalyst pumped through a resin bed in a counter current manner. Once exhausted, the resin bed is recharged with dilute sulfuric acid. The acid is completely utilized producing a stream of sodium sulphate and neutralized water. Rinse water from each stage is saved and reused for the next regeneration cycle or for rinsing. The sodium-sulfate-rich by-product waste can be harvested and sold as industrial-grade raw materials. The carbon dioxide generated at each ion exchange state is removed by a degasification step.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sulfuric acid
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Current system capacity: 30,000 bpd; Final system capacity: 90,000 bpd capacity

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system treats the produced water in the following sequence: advanced filtration through a cartridge filter, weak acid cation ion exchange softener with HCl addition to remove polyvalent cations, UV oxidation to disinfect the water, low-pressure reverse osmosis (RO), and high-pressure RO. After each RO step, the permeate is sent to effluent discharge. The remaining reject from the high pressure RO is sent to an optional evaporator. The distillate from the evaporate is sent as part of the effluent discharge, and the remaining concentrated brine or solids are disposed of separately.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Weak acid cation ion exchange softener: HCl; Between the two reverse osmosis steps: scale inhibitor

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The produced water, removed of most salvageable oil, first undergoes induced gas flotation, followed by walnut shell filtration for the purpose of de-oiling the feed water. The de-oiled water is cooled from 200 to 165 degrees Fahrenheit and degasified with the addition of acid to remove carbon dioxide, hydrogen sulfide, and excess alkalinity. The degasified water is softened in a multi-stage chemical softening process, which generates dense crystalline solids that are disposed of separately. The remaining water is cooled to 100 degrees Fahrenheit and treated with a multi-media filtration, weak acid cation exchange softening (in sodium form), and cartridge filtration, all at elevated pH, to further reduce hardness, metals, and particulate concentrations. This pretreated water is then pressurized through a double-pass reverse osmosis (RO) system to reduce TDS, silica, boron, and organics. A portion of the RO permeate is used for a nearby cooling tower to offset evaporation and blowdown and the remaining permeate is neutralized with sulfuric acid and carbon dioxide, and calcium chloride is injected to control the sodium adsorption ratio. The treated water is discharged to aquifer recharge basins via post-treatment constructed wetlands. The wetlands use a clay liner to prevent percolation of water in the aquifer and are planted with native flora, such as cattail.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Degasification: acid (unspecified); Permeate neutralization: sulfuric acid, carbon dioxide, and calcium chloride.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Desalination facility is designed to process 66,700 barrels per day of produced water.
MANUFACTURER: Chevron U.S.A and Veolia Water Solutions & Technologies

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Innovative approach of using a two-stage ion exchange to remove sulfate from a lime plant effluent stream that is directed to a tailings pond. In the first stage, a strong acid cation resin selectively removes calcium and magnesium from the process feed.  Sulfuric acid is then fed to the column to regenerate the resin, which releases the cations. The released calcium reacts with the sulfate to form solid gypsum and precipitates from solution. In the second stage, a weak base anion resin selectively removes sulfate from the process feed. Lime is then fed to the column to regenerate the resin, which releases the sulfate. The released sulfate reacts with the dissolved calcium to form solid gypsum and precipitates from solution. In both stages, the gypsum is separated and filtered. The solid by-product can then be shipped off-site for disposal or reuse.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Lime plant effluent stream flow rate: 91 m3/h (400 gpm)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Innovative approach of using a two-stage ion exchange to remove sulfate from the discharge of a tailings storage facility at a copper and gold mine in South East Asia. In the first stage, a strong acid cation resin selectively removes calcium and magnesium from the process feed.  Sulfuric acid is then fed to the column to regenerate the resin, which releases the cations. The released calcium reacts with the sulfate to form solid gypsum and precipitates from solution. In the second stage, a weak base anion resin selectively removes sulfate from the process feed. Lime is then fed to the column to regenerate the resin, which releases the sulfate. The released sulfate reacts with the dissolved calcium to form solid gypsum and precipitates from solution. In both stages, the gypsum is separated and filtered. The solid by-product can then be shipped off-site for disposal or reuse.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Plant flow rate: 800 m3/h (3,500 gpm)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Fluidized Bed reactor under anaerobic conditions followed by microfiltration.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: MicroCg, 1.5 % Phosphoric acid, Metsource micronutrients
MANUFACTURER: System - Envirogen Technologies, MicroCg - Environmental Operating Solutions, 1.5 % Phosphoric acid - Univar USA Inc, Metsource - Riverbend Labs
OANDM_COST: $2.4M annually (estimate)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Two-stage suspended and fixed film biological treatment followed by secondary clarification. The secondary treatment unit process consisted of three components: (1) pump station, (2) chemical pre-treatment, and (3) dissolved air flotation unit (referred to as DGF in the article). The pump station was designed to transfer biologically treated wastewater from a rotating biological contractor (RBC) basin to the flash/floc tank. The chemical pretreatment unit consists of a chemical metering unit and a flash/floc tank with two treatment cells. The wastewater then flows to a dissolved air flotation unit. The unit was designed for service as both a secondary clarifier (air) and a future oil removal process (nitrogen).
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Coagulant is added to the DGF influent by the refinery in the chemical pretreatment unit, polymer is added to the second compartment to flocculate biological solids. At a wastewater flow rate of 3.79 m3/min, the chemical feed system can dose polymer at approximately 0.45 ppm to 45 ppm to the flash/floc tank.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The DGF was designed so the WWTP can treat the 100th percentile of flow without exceeding the maximum specified CGC hydraulic or solids loading rates of 34.6 m/day and 97.8 kg/day/m2 respectively. At a MLSS concentration of 2,500 mg/L, the solids loading rate is the controlling design parameter.
MANUFACTURER: Environmental Treatment Systems, Model RT-350LA DGF

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Four 8” x 48” high vessels each filled with Sorbster adsorbent media (made of activated alumina) and operated in series at 1 pgm. The unit was equipped with water circulation pumping, flow control and pressure, pH, temperature and conductivity monitoring. Water inlet and outlet was sampled daily and tested for contaminant removal.
Activated Sludge Unit treating influent with dissolved desalter brine

New GEM hybrid centrifugal-dissolved air flotation system was tested to replace an older, larger DAF unit.  Chemical precipitation and sand trap precede the GEM unit, walnut filters replaced sand filters after the GEM unit.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: 2.5 ppm cationic polyacrylamide flocculant, 2.5 ppm anionic polyacrylamide flocculant

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The mostly-passive pilot treatment system consists of a biochemical reactor (BCR) and an aerobic polishing cell (APC). The BCR consists of a geomembrane-lined cell and filled with a buffered organic substrate that provides an organic carbon source for microbial population and promotes biological reduction of sulfate to sulfide and subsequent removal of metals in the BCR as metal sulfides precipitate. Treated effluent from the BCR flows directly into the APC, a polyethylene lined aeration channel designed to increase dissolved oxygen and manganese removal, as well as diminish effluent toxicity prior to discharge into a nearby tributary.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Average Temperature (deg. C): 5.60 (BCR Influent), 11.47 (APC effluent).

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Fluidized Bed Reactor (FBR) unit consisted of a 0.5 meter diameter by 4.5 meter high, stainless steel column filled with 182 kg of GAC media for biomass growth, followed by Skid mounted MBBR system with HDPE carrier media for biomass growth to 40% of tank volume.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: MicroCg, Phosphoric acid, Metsource, ammonium sulfate
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 60 min HRT
MANUFACTURER: Envirogen Technologies (FBR pilot unit); World Water Works (MBBR pilot unit)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Ion exchange (IX) system included an influent pump, bag filters to remove influent solids, IX units, effluent tank, brine waste storage tank, and regeneration system. The system consisted of 5 vessels (4 in series) - 2 organic pretreatment units followed by 3 selenium removal units. All five IX units used during the study were Siemens Simplex Softener units, each 24-inch diameter and 72-inch high and contained roughly 9 cubic feet of active media (Purolite A860 for the organic pretreatment units, Purolite A300 for the selenium removal units).
MEDIA_TYPE: Purolite A860 (organic pretreatment) and A300 (selenium removal)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 7 gpm
MANUFACTURER: Siemens Simplex Softener Units with Purolite resins

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Two ZVI reactor tanks in a series in a lead-lag configuration; each tank containing 1,100 pounds of ZVI media.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: pH adjustment - CO2 and sulfuric acid as needed
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 6-7 gpm

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Process wastewater from three waste streams (truck washing station, slaughtering and cutting unit, meat packing unit) go through mechanical pre-treatment separately. The waste streams are then combined for flow and freight balancing and are sent to the DAF.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Average chemical consumptions are 40 g/m3 FeCl3 (destabilization and coagulation) and 5 g/m3 polymer (flocculation)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Each DAF unit has 350 gpm capacity.
OANDM_COST: 0.6 Euro/m3 for chemicals, 0.18 kWh/m3 for electricity. Average operator attention time is two hours per day.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Mechanical pre-treatment is done in two stages. The first stage is coarse screening with a multi-rake bar screen RakeMax designed to protect the treatment plant from impairment by larger objects. The second stage consists of a couple of Rotamat Rotary drum screens (greasy layers are removed from the screens using a travelling high-pressure spray nozzle).  Wastewater is next pumped to a DAF unit where it is chemically pre-treated in a tubular reactor within the DAF unit.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Average consumptions are 85 g/m3 Polyaluminumchloride (PAC), 80 g/m3 NaOH, and 3.5 g/m3 polymer.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: DAF unit capacity = 28 l/s (430 gpm). MBR total membrane surface is 7,200 m2 and peak capacity is 28 l/s (430 gpm).
OANDM_COST: Chemical costs 0.72 €/m³, power consumption 0.7 kWh/m³. Operated by a single employee.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Mechanical pre-treatment consists of a vertical Rotamat screw screen to remove packing material. The screened wastewater is pumped to a buffer tank for flow equalization and then to a DAF unit with chemical pre-treatment.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: FeCl3 for emulsion breaking and coagulation (average - 110 g/m3), HNO3 (80 g/m3) or NaOH (265 g/m3) for neutralization and a polymer for flocculation (26 g/m3)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: DAF unit capacity is 110 m3/h (480 gpm).
OANDM_COST: Chemical costs 0.68 Euro/m3, power consumption 0.28 kWh/m3. Operated by a single employee.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Pretreatment systems followed by conventional activated sludge with dissolved air flotation as secondary clarification.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Designed to operate at a 95th percentile solids loading rate of 12.2 kg MLSS/hour/square meter.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: PW Unit#1: produced water enters the system and passes through a single filtration vessel to remove any residual solids. A mixing educator and volumetric feeder are then used to continuously add Osorb into the water stream. The produced water and Osorb are passed through two agitation tanks in series, where a combination of mechanical agitation and educator nozzles are applied. After the capture of solubles inside the mixing vessels, the Osorb and treated water pass over a vibratory separator to collect the organic-laden Osorb from the water discharge stream. RegenUnit#1: a double cone vacuum dryer, thermal fluid controller, vacuum pump, and condenser. After the Osorb captures soluble from produced water in PWUnit#1, it is transferred to RegenUnit#1 for regeneration. It is then ready for reuse in the pilot treatment systems to treat additional produced water.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 246 L/min
MANUFACTURER: ABS Materials, Inc, Produced Water Absorbents, Inc.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: DAF for solids separation followed by a membrane bioreactor. No details of either system included in the article.
Pre-screening, mixing and balancing tank, Huber DAF plant (chemical precipitation and flocculation), nitrification, two Huber VRM 20/300 membrane filtration plants, 150 m3 permeate storage tank
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: caustic soda added to mixing & balancing tank
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: DAF plant designed for the maximum flow of 60 m3/hr. MBRs have 12.5 m3/hr throughput capacity and 900 m2 membrane surface each.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The pilot system was a skid-mounted system and GE's ZeeWeed system was used as the MBR technology. The technology is a hollow-fiber, submerged membrane system that uses low pressure vacuum filtration to separate effluent (permeate) from mixed liquor suspended solids. Wastewater was pumped with a peristaltic pump from the reactor tank to the membrane tank, and solids were recycled from the membrane tank to the reactor tank by gravity. Permeate was drawn from the membrane tank through the membranes using a reversible gear drive pump (i.e. the permeate pump), which operated at a negative pressure. Permeate was discharged into the permeate collection tank prior to gravity discharge to drain.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Citric acid and sodium hypochlorite were alternated every 2-4 days as cleaning solutions.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The pilot system was a skid-mounted system and GE's ZeeWeed system was used as the MBR technology. TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Anaerobic FBR followed by an Aerobic FBR in series. The anaerobic FBR unit was constructed of a 14-foot diameter fiberglass tank and was 21-feet high. The media was GAC. The aerobic FBR unit was constructed of a 14-foot diameter fiberglass tank, 19-feet high, with a GAC media bed.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: ammonia, phosphate, sodium benzoate
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 20 gpm - normal operation flow, 45 gpm - design flow

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system consists of a stainless steel FBR system, 7.5 feet in diameter and 16 feet tall, with sand as the medium. The biological system is the last step of a longer treatment train that removes organics and metals upstream.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Acetic acid (up to 50% wt.) as an electron donor and phosphoric acid solution (up to 75% wt.) as a nutrient to the system
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design flow rate: 350 gallons per minute

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater passes through the following stages of treatment: 4 parallel first stage FBRs (#1-4), 14 feet diameter x 30 feet straight side with sand media; 4 parallel second stage FBRs (#5-8), 14 feet diameter x 26 feet straight side with GAC media; one aeration tank (14 feet diameter x 24.5 feet straight side); two DAF vessel assemblies, 10.5 ft. W X 10.5 ft. H X 40 ft. overall length; and two filter press assemblies, 80 cubic feet each.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Feed water is combined with recycle flow, ethanol, nutrients solution and pH control solution (25% caustic soda) in the first stage. Denatured ethanol is used as the biological food source, the nutrient for the biological reaction consists of a 39% urea/di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) solution.  The second stage flow is also combined with ethanol, nutrients, and caustic.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 1000 gpm total flow rate

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Anaerobic FBR pilot system followed by filtration. The FBR unit was two feet in diameter, 13.5 feet tall with GAC as the bed media.
MEDIA_TYPE: FBR media: GAC. Filter media not specified.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: MicroCg used as an electron donor in the FBR; phosphoric acid, micronutrients also added to the FBR. Coagulant and polymer were added to the wastewater prior to the filtration step.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 8 gpm flow rate, hydraulic residence time of 27 minutes.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system consisted of an MBR unit (aeration tank + membrane tank) and an RO unit in series. The feed water to the MBR was the discharge from the original cloth disc filter (the only treatment step after effluent is discharged from the mill). The RO system was a single-module, 4-inch system with concentrate stream recirculated to RO feed to improve water recovery.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 4 gpm flow rate. The MBR was started with a flux rate of 18 GFD (gallons per square foot per day) and ended with a flux of 30 GFD.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Polyferric sulfate (PFS) is added to the influent in two steps along with sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl). The influent flows to a solids thickener for solids removal and then to a reaction tank followed by two parallel settling ponds for polishing before the treated water effluent was discharged to an infiltration basin.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: PFS addition in two steps, NaOCl addition to increase oxidation state of arsenic so it will precipitate with ferric hydroxide, and sodium hydroxide addition to adjust settling pond pH.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: pH above 8 in settling ponds.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The wastewater treatment plant process design consists of a single train API separator, equalization tank, storm water tank, diversion tank, an Activated Sludge Unit (ASU) with an oxidation ditch configuration and brush aerator oxygen supply system, a secondary clarifier, and 3 non-aerated polishing lagoons in series. To maximize the wastewater treatment capacity while utilizing existing infrastructure, a project was completed to add a new fine bubble diffused air system to an old, out-of-service secondary clarifier and convert it into a Complete Mix Batch Reactor (CMBR). The CMBR was designed to operate in a number of modes, including in batch or continuous mode of operation, to increase capacity of the ASU and as an isolated sidestream chemostat reactor.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 0.8 MGD flow

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The mine water treatment and recovery system (MWTRS) is based on a high-density sludge (HDS) process that uses both a lime slurry and soda ash (Na2CO3) solution to remove dissolved metals from the mine water.  In Reactor A, soda ash and lime are mixed with and adhere to recycled solids from the thickener. This sludge mixture flows to Reactor B and is mixed with influent mine water and additional soda ash. The soda ash promotes the removal of dissolved calcium as CaCO3, largely on the surface of the recycled solids. Both reactors are mechanically mixed. The wastewater continues into a thickener, where optional polymer is added to encourage the sludge separation. A sludge recycling pump helps segregate recycled sludge to reactor A and waste sludge for disposal. Overflow from the thickener is discharged (i.e., sent by pipeline for irrigation).
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Soda ash (300-900 mg/L), lime, Nalco 83400 liquid flocculant (10-15mg/1,000 gallons)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design flow: 160 L/s (2,500 gpm)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Feed, including corn, wheat, and other organic waste, along with recycled sludge, is treated in a thermophilic digester. Effluent from the digester is mixed with raw pig manure and sent to a screw press, where biosolids are formed into cakes and sold as fertilizer. Effluent from the screw press is sent through an ultrafiltration (UF) membrane with an anti-fouling vortex generator, where retained solids are returned to the digester. Effluent from the membrane system is treated through reverse osmosis (RO) for reuse or discharged as an unspecific outflow.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: System flow: 75 m3/day; Average operating temperature of digester: 55 degrees Celsius

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Mixed feed, including pig manure, corn, wheat, and other organic waste, along with recycled sludge, is treated in a thermophilic digester. Effluent from the digester is sent to a screw press, where biosolids are formed into cakes and sold as fertilizer. Effluent from the screw press is sent through an ultrafiltration (UF) membrane with an anti-fouling vortex generator, where retained solids are returned to the digester. Effluent from the membrane system is treated through reverse osmosis (RO) for reuse or discharged as an unspecific outflow.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: System flow: 93 m3/day; Average operating temperature of digester: 45 degrees Celsius

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Raw wastewater is screened using disk filters, micro or ultrafiltration, weak acid cation exchange, and then reverse osmosis.

The system treats a combination of biological treatment system effluent and cooling tower blowdown. The treatment train includes a blend feed tank, oxidation for manganese and copper removal, dual media filtration, granular activated carbon (GAC) for organics removal, cartridge filtration, ultrafiltration (UF), ultraviolet (UV) disinfection, reverse osmosis (RO) with acid feed, and degasification to remove carbon dioxide.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) for manganese and copper removal
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow = 15,000 cmd combined from cooling tower (5,000 cmd) and organic wastewater treatment system (OWWTS) (10,000 cmd)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The treatment train includes a primary clarifier, dissolved air flotation (DAF), activated sludge aeration basin, secondary clarifier, ultrafiltration (UF), and reverse osmosis (RO). The UF system uses submerged ZeeWeed 500b membranes configured in 7 parallel trains with 11 cassettes in each train. The RO permeate is reused in the refinery for boiler feed.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Designed for peak flow = 26,000 m3/d

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system includes a membrane bioreactor (MBR) using submerged ultrafiltration (UF) membrane. The system was installed in two phases. During the first phase, two MBR trains with six cassettes of ZeeWeed 500d membrane were installed. During the second phase, four MBR trains with eight cassettes of ZeeWeed 500d were installed.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow capacity = 20,000 m3/d

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Approximately 4,800m3/d of heavily contaminated groundwater is pretreated by oil/water separation, oxidation, coagulation, high-rate clarification, sand filtration, and granular ferric hydroxide adsorption (for arsenic removal).  The pretreated water is then combined 2,400 m3/d of contaminated groundwater and fed to the membrane bioreactor (MBR) system, which includes pre-denitrification, nitrification, and post-denitrification tanks, and four ZeeWeed 500d trains. The MBR effluent is then fed directly to a three-train reverse osmosis (RO) system. Finally, the RO reject stream is treated by a granular activated carbon (GAC) system prior to discharge.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: MBR designed flow = 7,200 m3/d; MBR average flow = 5,289 m3/d; GAC designed flow = 2,160 m3/day; Recycled water production = 5,040 m3/d

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The Selenium Treatment System (STS) consisted of the following series of treatment cells: (1) vertical downflow bioreactor, (2) vertical upflow wetland, (3) subsurface flow wetland, and (4) subsurface flow wetland. The 0.16-acre vertical downflow bioreactor is constructed of 60-mil HDPE liner and bed of enriched organic substrate over a bed of limestone, with water ponded to approximately 3-ft above the substrate. The 0.14-acre vertical upflow wetland is constructed of 60-mil HDPE liner and bed of sphagnum peat moss over a bed of limestone, with water ponded near the surface of the peat substrate. The 0.16-acre subsurface flow wetland is constructed of pulsed-flow emergent wetland (e.g., cattails or bulrush) in a bed of limestone, with water ponded at varying heights throughout the day (<1.0 ft below the bed to 0.5 ft above the bed). The 0.11-acre subsurface flow wetland is constructed of emergent wetland (e.g., cattails or bulrush) at a depth of 1 foot in native topsoil.
MEDIA_TYPE: Vertical downflow bioreactor: mixture of composted manure, sawdust, wood chips, hay/straw, peat, and limestone chips
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Effluent temperature ranged from 17 to 26 degrees Celsius.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Two horizontal roughing filters were constructed to compare two filter media: gravel and charcoal. The filter medium was placed in different filter chambers. The compartment was filled up with medium sizes of 15mm-5mm decreasing in size in the direction of flow. The filter beds were provided with under drain systems, so that it will allow cleaning of the filters after a certain period. Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) was used as a performance monitoring parameter. Researchers noted that after 4 to 5 weeks of use, the filters "ripened" as biofilm layers developed around the coarse media, which improved the filter’s ability to remove TDS.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: A constant filtration rate of 1 m/h was used.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The pilot-scale continuous flow operation system consisted of an equalization tank, an anaerobic baffled reactor (ABR), and a biofilm airlift suspension reactor (BASR). The ABR contained a series of vertical baffles to separate the reactor into five equal compartments. The BASR contained spherical ceramic materials that were employed as biocarriers to facilitate the development of biofilm on the biocarrier surface.

Furthermore, to obtain a final effluent free of suspended solids, the treated saline was delivered for diaphragm electrolysis after residual particles were removed by DrM filter.

The wastewater is then treated with a biological aerated filter (BAF) unit, which is composed of five separate reactors filled with polyurethane foam as a carrier and inoculated with activated sludge from a municipal sewage treatment plant.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The complete-mix activated sludge process consisted of a 20-L aeration tank and 4-L clarifier. The aeration tank was aerated using fine-bubble aerators connected to aquarium pumps and heated using a submerged aquarium heater.  The mixed liquor from the aeration tank flowed by gravity to the clarifier. The effluent flowed over an unbaffled weir to an effluent tank. The settled sludge was then pumped back to the aeration tank continuously.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: ballasted flocculation and lamellar tube effect high rate clarification. The pilot-scale test included one mobile clarification unit. The mobile clarification unit consists of coagulation, ballasted flocculation with microsand, settling in a lamellar tube clarifier, with microsand recovery in a hydrocyclone. The unit first treats the wastewater by adding a coagulant (alum or ferric chloride) and a  polymer (a flocculant aid) to destabilize the particles. The particles then adhere to injected microsand in the system by polyelectrolyte bridging. The pumped slurry then enters the lamellar tube clarifier where the microsand/sludge settles. The settled microsand/sludge then enters the hydrocyclones, where the lighter sludge is discharged and the heavier sand is recovered for reuse, and injected by gravity back into the system.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Alum, ferric chloride, polymer
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design flow rate: 700-1,000 gpm; Test flow rate: 900-950 gpm

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The field-scale test included five mobile clarification units. The mobile clarification unit consists of coagulation, flocculation, and settling. The unit first treats the wastewater by adding a coagulant (alum or ferric chloride) and a polymer (a flocculant aid) to destabilize the particles. The particles then adhere to injected microsand in the system by polyelectrolyte bridging. The pumped slurry then enters the clarifier where the microsand/sludge settles. The settled microsand/sludge then enters the hydrocyclones, where the lighter sludge is discharged and the heavier sand is injected by gravity back into the system.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Alum, ferric chloride, polymer
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Total flow rate of all 5 units: 4,000-5,000 gpm

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The influent from the industrial wastewater treatment plant was directed to a 1,000 gallon holding tank from which wastewater was pumped into the electrocoagulation (EC) unit using iron plates. Sulfuric acid was added to the influent to lower the pH.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sulfuric acid

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The influent from the industrial wastewater treatment plant was directed to a 1,000 gallon holding tank from which wastewater was pumped into the electrocoagulation (EC) unit using aluminum plates. Sodium hydroxide is added to the influent to increase the pH.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium Hydroxide

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The existing treatment system consists of a sour water stripper, extractor, ammonia stripper, ammonia distillation column, and solvent distillation column. The coal-gasification wastewater is introduced into the sour water stripper in two streams:  one is preheated by the bottom stream of sour water stripper and fed to the middle of the stripper, and the other is cooled to about 45 °C in a cooler and fed to the top of the stripper to chill the top vapor stream. Sour gas consisting of CO2 and H2S is stripped out from the top of the stripper. The stream from the bottom of the stripper is pumped to the top of the extractor. Meanwhile, diisopropyl ether (DIPE) is fed, as extraction solvent, to the bottom of the countercurrent extractor to extract phenol. The extract from the top of the extractor is fed to solvent distillation column to separate DIPE from phenol. The raffinate from the bottom of the extractor is fed to the ammonia stripper. Dissolved DIPE in the raffinate is recovered from the top of the ammonia stripper. Ammonia is stripped from the side-draw of ammonia stripper and then refined by a system of two flash tanks and an ammonia distillation column. The treated water is discharged from the bottom of the ammonia stripper and sent to an unspecified biological treatment system.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Ammonia Stripper: Sodium Hydroxide; Extractor: DIPE (Diisopropyl ether)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The new treatment system consists of a wastewater stripper, extractor, solvent stripper, and solvent distillation column. The coal-gasification wastewater is introduced into the stripper in two streams:  one is preheated and fed to the middle of the stripper, and the other is cooled and fed to the top of the stripper. Sour gas is stripped out from the top of the stripper. When the temperature in the stripper is properly controlled, ammonia accumulates in the vapor phase of the middle of the stripper. The ammonia-rich gas is drawn from the middle side and sent to a sequence of three flash tanks. Ammonia is produced from the top of flash tanks, while a stream of aqueous volatile phenol is separated from the bottom of the flash tanks and sent to a settle tank. The wastewater, removed sour gas, and ammonia are produced from the bottom of the stripper, cooled to around 45 °C, and sent to the top of the countercurrent extractor. Meanwhile, to remove phenol, diisopropyl ether (DIPE) as the extraction solvent is fed to the bottom of the extractor. The extract from the top of extractor is fed to a solvent distillation column to separate DIPE from phenol. The raffinate from the bottom of extractor is fed to a solvent stripper. Dissolved DIPE in the raffinate is stripped and recovered from the top of the solvent stripper. The treated water is discharged from the bottom of the solvent stripper and sent to an unspecified biological treatment system.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Wastewater Stripper: Sodium Hydroxide; Extractor: DIPE

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION:
The treatment system consisted of the following components: 
1. Chemical oxidation was carried out in a continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR). The reactor (vertical cylindrical vessel with flat bottom) was 0.16 m in diameter and its overall height was 0.38 m. The working volume and the overall volume of the reactor were 7.0 dm3 and 7.4 dm3, respectively. The static liquid height was 0.36 m.
2. Neutralization was carried out in a stirred tank similar to the reactor described above (with 7 dm3 capacity).
3. Solid–liquid separation was conducted in a lamellar settler with 22 dm3 capacity.
4. Six storage tanks: (i) for OMW (32 dm3 capacity), (ii) for the oxidant reagent (3 dm3 capacity), (iii) for the catalyst (3 dm3 capacity), (iv) for the neutralizing agent (3 dm3), (v) for the preparation of the flocculant provided with agitation system (1 dm3 capacity), and (vii) for the final treated water (50 dm3 capacity).
5. Nine peristaltic pumps.
6. Pneumatic level sensors.
7. Three stirring system formed by overhead stirrers installed in the oxidation reactor, neutralization tank, and flocculant storage tank.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: In the CSTR, H2O2 (5% w/v) and FeCl3 (8% v/v) were used as oxidant and catalyst in Fenton’s reaction. In the neutralization/flocculation tank, the pH is adjusted by a programmable logic controller using NaOH (1M) to target values within the range 6–7, and the flocculant (1 mg dm-3 of Nalco 77171) is added. Other reagents (phenol and HCl) are mentioned; however, it is unclear if and when they are added to the system.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Optimum CSTR operation values were: pH = 3 achieved by the addition of the catalyst (without acid addition when [FeCl3]/[H2O2] > 0.01), Tmin = 3 h, [FeCl3]/[H2O2] ratio from 0.026 to 0.058 w/w upon Fe(III) concentration ranging between 0.35 and 0.40 g dm-3, and ambient temperature.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater from a food waste treatment facility was fed through the system consisting of a thermophilic two-phase anaerobic digestion reactor, chemical precipitation step, and shortcut biological nitrogen removal reactor (SBNR). The anaerobic digester consisted of an acid phase for pre-fermentation and a gas phase for anaerobic digestion. Polymer is then added to the digested wastewater in a mixing tank, which is then stirred and allowed to settle in a storage tank. The wastewater is then pumped through the SBNR. The SBNR reactor used a four-stage post-denitrification process in order to enhance nutrient (TN and TP) removal efficiency. This process was comprised of two anoxic reactors (anoxic-1, anoxic-2) mixed by stirrers at 60 rpm and two aerobic reactors (aerobic-1, aerobic-2) mixed by aeration. The treated wastewater then went to a settling tank where suspended solids were captured to produce clear effluent and to provide concentrated sludge underflow for recycling and wasting. The anaerobic digester consisted of a 1.2 m3 acid phase reactor for pre-fermentation and a 4.2 m3 gas phase reactor for anaerobic digestion. The volume of chemical coagulation reactor was 0.28 cubic meters. In the SBNR, the effective volumes of the anoxic and aerobic reactors were 0.24 m3 and 0.48 m3, respectively.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: A commercial polymer known as Praestol Alum was added to the mixing tank (after anaerobic digestion) with constant dosage of 90 mg/L.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The wastewater from the stabilization tanks is introduced into two parts: one heated by the feed-bottoms heat exchanger and fed in the middle of the sour water stripper, which is the heat feed, and the other cooled and fed to the top of the stripper. The sour gas is removed overhead. When the temperature in the stripper is properly controlled, the NH3 is accumulated in the middle of the stripper and exists in the liquid phase with a high ammonia concentration and in the vapor phase with rich ammonia. The ammonia-rich gas is drawn from the middle side. Then, it is further purified through a three-step condensation. Refined ammonia of 99% concentration is obtained, while the condensate is recycled to the hot feed. When a large amount of acid gas and ammonia is removed from the wastewater, the pH value of the bottom stream is effectively reduced below 7, thus greatly improving the extraction performance.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The side-draw is located at the 28th tray. The stripper is operated in following conditions: the cold feed temperature is between 35 to 40 °C, the cold feed/hot feed ration is 0.2 to 0.4, the top pressure is 0.6 MPa, and the side draw/feed mass ratio is 9% to 13%, respectively.
OANDM_COST: 9.5M yuan/year

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Iron co-precipitation pilot test treated stripped sour water. The system consists of absorbing selenium species to a ferrihydrite floc. The influent was pretreated with hydrogen peroxide to oxidize selenide to selenite, which encouraged adsorption. The pretreatment was followed by ferric chloride addition, where selenite was subsequently adsorbed to ferrihydrite floc under undescribed conditions, and settling and flotation, which removed the ferric hydroxide floc. The effluent is then discharged to the refinery's existing wastewater treatment system (WWTS), which consists of equalization, dissolved gas flotation, aeration, and clarification.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Hydrogen peroxide, ferric chloride
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Temperature: 35 degrees Celsius; Hydrogen peroxide hydraulic retention time (HRT): 2-4 hours; Ferric chloride HRT: 15-30 minutes

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The granular media filtration pilot test treated the refinery’s existing wastewater treatment system (WWTS) effluent. The existing WWTS consists of equalization, dissolved gas flotation, aeration, and clarification. The filtration system is sized for mercury particles between 3 µm to 7 µm.
Trailer-mounted ABMet bioreactor system and supporting equipment. The ABMet system is an attached-growth downflow filter that uses microbes cultured within the GAC bed to create anoxic conditions.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The existing wastewater treatment system accepted refinery wastewater through an equalization tank and initially processed the water through a dissolved air flotation (DAF) unit. Water from the DAF unit was split to three parallel complete mix activated sludge (CMAS) units. The pilot study added a microfiltration unit which accepted screened sludge from the CMAS. Effluent from the microfiltration was tested.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Refinery wastewater is collected in a sump and conveyed by gravity sewer to a lift station, which pumps the wastewater to two American Petroleum Institute (API) oil-water separators. Effluent from the API separators flows by gravity to two dissolved air flotation (DAF) clarifiers. Effluent from the DAF units is transferred to a sequencing batch reactor (SBR) system for aerobic biological removal of dissolved organic compounds and nitrogen. The SBR system includes a surge tank and two SBR units. Effluent from the SBR system is transferred to rotating disk cloth filters to remove solids prior to discharge. Discharge TSS concentration is 29 mg/L

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Feed pumps to a 2-stage system of packed-bed, fixed-film anaerobic digesters.  Each stage has 6 bioreactors.  Effluent from stage one goes to stage two.  Stage two effluent is pumped to effluent storage tank and then commingled with other plant effluents in a pond prior to Outfall 001. Reactors periodically backwashed with stored treated effluent to remove accumulated reduced metals, suspended solids, and biomass. Backwash is routed to separate, existing treatment system.

Pretreatment includes a screw press, where solids are removed and disposed offsite. The feed water is then concentrated in a batch mode for 4 hours, reaching a solid content of 13%, to ensure anti-fouling success. The proprietary pilot-scale system recovered 77.2% of the water from the original process water, compared to the initial value of 4.1%.

Side-streams are also sent to the recycle system directly from the manufacturing facility. The recycle system starts with an equalization tank. The treatment process begins with a two-stage chemical softening and coagulation system, followed by tubular microfiltration and reverse osmosis (RO) systems. RO permeate is returned to the cooling tower for reuse at the manufacturing plant and the reject stream is discharged to an on-site evaporation pond.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: A coagulant (ferric sulphate) and flocculant (cationic polymer) were added via a mixing tube to influent from an oil sands mining tailings pond. The wastewater was then pumped to a vertical-flow configuration dissolved air filtration unit followed by an ultrafiltration (UF) process. The UF unit consisted of an immersed hollow-fibre membrane unit operated in tank-drain mode. Membranes were thin-film polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), with a nominal pore size of 0.04 um. Treated water from the UF process flowed to a reverse osmosis (RO) system. The RO system consisted of a spiral-wound, thin-film membrane operated at constant flux (10-20 gfd).

An organic dispersant (unknown dose) was added to the RO system to help reduce organic fouling of the membrane.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The UF unit had a membrane area of 500 sqft and was rated for net flow rates of 5-225 US gpm. The RO system had operating pressures of up to 400 psi. Influent water temperatures varied from 4 to 14 degrees C.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: A coagulant (ferric sulphate) and flocculant (cationic polymer) were added via a mixing tube to influent from an oil sands mining tailings pond. The wastewater was then pumped to a vertical-flow configuration dissolved air filtration unit followed by multimedia filtration unit (MMF). The MMF is a manually-backwashed pressurized column filter with anthracite, sand, and garnet beds. The effluent then flows to an advanced oxidation process (AOP) that uses ozone and peroxide to generate hydroxyl radicals that break down organics.

ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Operating pressures for the MMF unit varied between 15 and 50 psi. Influent water temperatures varied from 4 to 14 degrees C.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The moving bed bioreactor (MBBR) utilized two 1500 gallon tanks with suspended plastic media. The upstream tank was operated in anoxic mode, with a mean dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration of 0.75 mg/L and equipped with a mixer. The downstream tank was aerated and operated in aerobic mode, with a mean DO of 6.8 mg/L. A recirculation loop from the aerobic tank back to the anoxic tank was operated with recirculation rates of 0-3.5 times the net flow rate. A water heater was used to maintain influent water temperatures above 8C over the duration of the pilot.

Media packing density was approximately 55% by volume, with the media having a surface area of 400 m2/m3. Influent water temperatures varied from 4 to 14 degrees C.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The membrane bioreactor (MBR) consisted of a single-stage aerobic tank, with effluent drawn through hollow-fiber PVDF membranes with a total surface area of 10 square feet. Sludge was wasted periodically via a manual drain valve.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Prior to the constructed wetlands, the wastewater is pre-treated with vacuum filtration, primary and secondary clarifiers, and pressurized sand filtration. The constructed wetland area is approximately 2.1 acres and consists of three different cells: free water surface (FWS), vegetated submerged bed (VSB), and vertical flow bed (VFB). FWS cells consist of primarily emergent wetland and rooted aquatic plants and the wastewater is primarily treated in the plant stems and leaves, shallow soils, and associated microorganisms. VSB cells rely on gravel media that allows the wastewater to flow through the roots of emergent wetland plants with minimal surface water. VFB cells rely on the soil matrix, gravel media, and surface distribution mechanism that allows the wastewater to flow vertically through the soil and wetland plant roots without significant surface water accumulation. The constructed wetlands effluent is combined with cooling water blowdown prior to discharge.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system was designed to remove ammonia-nitrogen (NH3-N) and zinc (Zn2+) concentrations from refinery plant wastewater. The system first added sulfide wastewater or sulfide solution (Na2S) to precipitate zinc and then treated the supernatant in a stripping unit.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The absorption system consists of three pressure vessels operated in series and loaded with an adsorptive organic and inorganic crystal media with an affinity and capacity for copper. TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The DEamMONification System (DEMON-System) involves two process steps - the partial nitrification of ammonia and the subsequent anoxic oxidation of the residual ammonia and nitrite to nitrogen gas. About half the amount of ammonia is oxidized to nitrite; afterwards, residual ammonia and nitrite are anoxically transformed to elementary nitrogen gas. The total nitrogen removal is accomplished while using a stoichiometric oxygen demand of only 40 percent. The process is performed in a sequencing batch reactor plant in which the individual steps occur in timely structured occurrences. At first, the reactor is gradually filled with centrate and the content is alternately aerated and mixed. Nitritation then occurs during aerated periods while deammonification occurs during anoxic/anaerobic periods. The system is designed as a fully automated process with a patented control strategy. Finely tuned process controls are necessary in order to closely monitor operating parameters and to maintain consistent, high-quality effluent.

The system first treats wastewater influent with an anoxic bioreactor that uses influent COD as the biodegradable carbon source to remove nitrates from wastewater. A subsequent aerobic bioreactor recycles activated sludge to maximize COD removal.  The system removes organics in both the aeration and anoxic zones. The aeration zone uses air as its oxygen source, while the anoxic zone uses nitrates recycled from the aeration zone.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design rate of 3.4 m3/min (900 gal/min).

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Ultrafiltration (UF) system with hollow-fiber membrane cartridges pretreat water bound for RO treatment. UF system consists of 108 254-mm-diameter (10-in.-diameter) TARGA PMC membrane cartridges on six racks.

The system then combines the acidic and non-acidic waste streams and includes equalization, two-stage chemical precipitation (soda ash, sodium hydroxide, polymer, and sulfuric acid addition), multi-media filtration, granular activated carbon, ion exchange, reverse osmosis, and sludge dewatering.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: An electrochemical process in which wastewater contaminants respond to strong electric fields and electrically induced oxidation and reduction reactions.  It included 217 iron plates, each of which was 203 mm wide × 762 mm long × 3.18 mm thick (8 in. wide × 30 in. long × 0.125 in. thick). TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: A membrane bioreactor (MBR) combines an activated sludge reactor with membrane filtration. The treatment system consists of two equalization tanks, a bioreactor, and two membrane filtration tanks. After equalization, wastewater enters the aerobic bioreactor at a set flow rate. The bioreactor also receives reverse osmosis (RO) concentrate (supplies minerals or nutrients), a mixture of other supplemental micro and minor nutrients, and a 50% phosphoric acid solution.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION:

The DAF and BVF effluents will then be blended and sent to aerated lagoons, where existing aerators will aerobically treat the wastewater. The lagoon effluent then enters an aerobic SBR to remove more COD and provide
nitrification and partial denitrification. Methanol is added to the SBR effluent prior to denitrification filters which reduce the residual nitrate–nitrogen concentration.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Industrial wastewater is pretreated with disinfection-oxidization, coagulation-flocculation, sedimentation, a multimedia filter, and ultrafiltration.  It is then dechlorinated, passes through a cartridge filter and then passes through a two-pass reverse osmosis (RO) system. Finally the treated water flows through a mixed-bed ion exchange system to achieve the required boiler makeup water quality.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Washwater enters a trench drain and flows to a grit trap to collect particulates.  A hydrocyclone then removes solids.  An aeration tank increases oxygen before the water enters a sealed biochamber (with aerobic bacteria that degrade hydrocarbon-based materials, such as oils, detergents, and waxes).  Treated water enters a storage tank from which it can be reused or sent for ozonation and reverse-osmosis, depending on user needs.  All effluent is reused.

When the biochamber is not in use for extended periods, water is recirculated between it and the aeration tank to maintain bacterial activity.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Anaerobic effluent is sent through the following membrane bioreactor (MBR) system: earthen basins for aeration, a fine screen to remove any large material, and parallel membrane-filtration tanks. Each tank houses immersed hollow-fiber membrane cassettes through which permeate is extracted by centrifugal pumps. The concentrate is then returned to the aeration basins and the effluent is either returned for plant reuse or sent to the publically owned treatment works (POTW).

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The proposed membrane bioreactor (MBR) system includes: a carbon-steel aeration tank, blowers and coarse-bubble diffusers to provide air for membrane scouring, and two gravity fed tanks housing membrane cassettes. The concentrate would then be pumped back to the biological reactors and the effluent would either be reused for cooling tower makeup, other non-product applications, or discharged to the sewer.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: An oil- and shortening-production facility -- proposed treatment system consists of a dissolved air flotation (DAF) followed by a two phase biological process. Anaerobic, for biological phosphorus reduction followed by aeration and MBR. Sludge from the MBR is recirculated to the anaerobic tank. Waste sludge removes excess phosphorus. TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: This system begins a rotary drum screen, two equalization tanks (mixed), and a gas-energy mixing system (GEM), which combines centrifugal hydrocyclone and a dissolved air flotation (DAF) process. The GEM provides continuous flow mixing, in-line flocculation, and nucleation and entrainment of fine dissolved-air bubbles for efficient particulate removal.  Flow continues to two moving-bed biofilm reactors (MBBRs), a clarifier, and periodically pumped to another tank for further thickening.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system includes a tangential screen to remove large particles, oil-skimmer tank to remove floating oils, equalization tank with alkalinity supplementation (magnesium hydroxide), anaerobic reactor, and four anaerobic membrane bioreactor (MBR) tanks (seven submerged membrane units per tank).  The permeate is then discharged to a sequencing batch reactor (SBR) and nitrified before being sent off site for municipal wastewater treatment. The wastewater is then pumped through a motorized rotary drum screen to remove solids larger than 3mm before entering a holding tank, where nitrogen and phosphorus are added before the flow enters two membrane bioreactor (MBR) units. Each MBR unit consists of a flow-equalization chamber, a solids holding zone, and an aeration zone with submerged membrane modules. Solid wastes from the MBRs are dewatered with a belt filter press. Effluent from the MBRs enters an equalization tank before being discharged to a municipal system.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The treatment train includes a dissolved air flotation (DAF) unit followed by a static granular bed reactor (SGBR). THE SGBR consists of an influent storage tank, hydrogen sulfide gas scrubber system, reactor, effluent storage tank, and pipes along the bottom of the reactor for backwashing. The treated effluent is then discharged to an on-site lagoon.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater disinfection consists of a chlorine contact basin, chemical feed system, and post-aeration basin. Chlorine solution is injected into the treated wastewater at the head of the chlorine contact basin in a rapid-mix zone. The water then passes through a series of serpentines in the basin and flows over a weir into a dechlorination rapid-mix chamber, where sulfur dioxide solution is added to reduce chlorine levels below the permit discharge limit. The dechlorinated water then passes into a post-aeration basin, where its dissolved oxygen content is increased before the effluent is discharged into the river.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The raw wastewater was fed into the immersed ZeeWeed® UF membrane system. The ZeeWeed® UF unit was operated in a “feed and bleed” mode. In this operational mode, the ZeeWeed® UF unit was fed continuously with raw wastewater (feed) and at the same time a smaller amount of concentrated waste was rejected (bleed) from the bottom of the process tank and sent to drain. The bleed stream decreases the suspended solids and large colloidal material concentration within the membrane tank, which improves membrane performance. Intermittent aeration was used to scour the membrane surface and remove any fouling agents accumulated during operation. Permeate was drawn by the process pumps through the membrane pores by applying a gentle vacuum, while the suspended solids and large colloidal material remained in the membrane tank. The ZeeWeed® UF unit permeate was sent to the IX unit. The IX unit consisted of two vessels containing strong acid cation resin in the sodium cycle and operated in series. Each IX vessel was fed from the top of the resin bed and the treated water was collected at the bottom. The resin was regenerated using a brine solution that was fed at the bottom of the vessel and collected from the top. The spent brine solution was sent to drain. The frequency of resin regeneration depended on the ionic strength of the feed wastewater. The effluent from IX unit was fed to the RO unit. A two stage configuration was selected for the RO unit. The second stage RO reject was sent to drain, while the permeate from both stages was blended and considered as the pilot effluent. Two different RO membrane products were used during this pilot study, a Filmtec BW30-4040 membrane and two Hydranautics ESPA2-4040.
MEDIA_TYPE: UF unit: ZeeWeed 500c; IX: Amberlite IR-120; RO: Filmtec BW30-4040
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Citric acid and sodium hypochlorite were used for maintenance cleans in the UF system. Citric acid recovery clean concentration averaged 1000 mg/L. NaOCl recovery clean concentration averaged 1000 mg/L. An NaCl brine solution was added to the IX to regenerate the resin.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Trans-membrane pressure (TMP) of UF membrane averaged 18 kPa. The permeation cycle duration was 10 minutes. The net permeate flow rate averaged 1102 L/h, and the net flux rate averaged 15.8 L/m2h. IX feed flow rate averaged 1364 L/h, with a range of 606 - 1420 L/h. The RO feed flow rate was 386.0 L/h for both types of membranes. The permeate flow rate ranged from 193 - 212.3 L/h for the Filmtec membrane. The reject  flow rate ranged from 193 - 173.7 L/h for the Filmtec membrane. The TMP ranged from 550 - 895 kPa for the Filmtec membrane.
MANUFACTURER: UF unit: ZeeWeed 500c; IX: Amberlite IR-120; RO: Filmtec BW30-4040

Effluent was treated in a newly constructed humic acid addition system. EPA's water quality criterion for copper increases directly with increased concentration of dissolved organic carbon (DOC), according to EPA's biotic ligand model (BLM). Humic acid was added to increase the effluent DOC and thus the copper water quality criterion.

The treatment train includes an oil-water separator, an equalization tank, a clarifier, integrated fixed-film/activated sludge (IFAS), a secondary clarifier, and aerobic digestion. This original treatment train included two parallel bioreactors that were retrofitted with effluent screens and plastic carrier media.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The influent is derived from two streams: a segregated acid stream and a non-acid stream. The acid stream is first equalized, pre-treated with lime to remove sulfate as calcium sulfate, and then undergoes settling. Pretreatment reduces the TDS into the RO system. The acid stream is then combined with the non-acid stream. The combined streams are equalized and entered a two-stage settling/precipitation process at two different pH levels. The first stage (softening) reduces the calcium concentration. The second stage removes aluminum. The combined streams then underwent multi-media filtration, granular activated carbon, ion exchange (removes calcium and other multivalent metals), and reverse osmosis. The reverse osmosis permeate is then reused for cooling towers, boiler feed, and rinse water tank makeup. RO brine is evaporated and condensate mixed with permeate for reuse. Evaporated brine solids are disposed of off site.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium hydroxide, soda ash, polymer, sulfuric acid, lime, antiscalant prior to RO
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: To reduce growth of bacteria on the RO membranes, after system start up, sodium hypochlorite added at the headworks and added additional sanitizing and membrane cleaning.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The upgraded treatment train includes: a tailings pond, polishing pond, two reaction tanks and Actiflo system. The Actiflo system consists of a is a high rate settling process that combines the advantages of ballasted flocculation and lamella clarification with coagulants, microsand, and polymer addition. The upgraded system removed two reaction tanks and a conventional clarifier.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater passes through 150µ size grit handler for solids removal, an oil coalescer for free oil removal to mitigate membrane fouling, membrane biological reactor (MBR), and fixed bed absorption filters to remove arsenic and other selective metals. The membranes in the MBR are configured as small diameter tubules that are bundled in modules and housed in a cassette for easy handling. The membrane modules are immersed in the membrane tank, whereby wastewater passes concentrically into the membranes under a small vacuum induced by pumping versus under high pressure. This results in the solids being retained in the reactor, while the treated wastewater (permeate) is discharged. Every 10 to 12 minutes, the effluent pump is reversed for approximately 30 seconds to “back pulse” permeate back into the bioreactor; this helps to clear the membranes and thus prevent fouling while maintaining outflow.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: MBR: Urea and phosphoric acid add to provide nutrients for maintaining effective biodegradation. Nutrient dose required: 35 mg/L N and 7 mg/L P. NaOH was added to adjust pH.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow to MPT: 400 gpm; System Footprint: 3,500 ft2; MBR HRT: 0.6 days; flow through treatment system: 35 GPM
MANUFACTURER: MBR Design and Construction: Zenon Environmental, Inc. Arsenic Adsorption: Bayer AG, Bayoxide E33 ferric oxide.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater is pumped into the bottom of a mixer containing sulfuric acid and a tertiary amine in Tank 1. Cr(VI) is extracted as an oil-soluble salt and is sent, along with cleaned water, into a settler. Low-density Cr-rich extracted phase is sent to Tank 2. NaOH is added in Tank 2 to neutralize the extractant and convert the chromate to sodium chromate Na2CrO4. Regenerated extractant is recycled back to tank 1 and higher density chrome concentrate is captured.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: 25% NaOH at 10 gal/day was added to stripper S-1; 50% Sulfuric acid at 8 gal/day was added to extractor E-4.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The raw wastewater was pump aspirated to a fiberglass tank, which was transported to the university campus where the ozone treatment system was assembled. The experimental set-up for ozone treatment consisted of an air dryer, compressor, ozone generator and semi-batch reactor. The air dryer consisted of a column which was filled with highly adsorptive anhydrous SiO2. Ozone was generated using an ozonator at a concentration of 20 gm-3 (ozone:air). A water-cooling jacket was used to keep the reactor contents at constant temperature (20 C) and an ozone trap containing 4% potassium iodide solution was connected at the top of the reactor to collect all remaining ozone gas passing through the reactor. The ozone–air mixture (1m3 h-1) was fed into the reactor through a micro-porous plate gas sparger located at the base of the semi-batch reactor. All experiments were carried out in triplicate in an 18-L cylindrical semi-batch reactor. The reactor consisted of a polyvinyl chloride/polyethylene column of 0.15-m diameter, 1.0-m height and the flow rate of the textile wastewater was 0.45m^3 h-1. Ozonation at pH 3.0 was carried out after pH adjustment of the textile wastewater with 5M H2SO4. To maximize ozone transfer to the wastewater, the gas was sparged in countercurrent in relation to the textile wastewater circulation. Ozonation treatment/wastewater recirculation was carried out for 4 h, and after this period the color removal was lower.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: pH adjustment of the textile wastewater with 5M H2SO4 for the pH of 3.0 test run.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The system was run at pH levels entered above. The system performed better at a pH of 9.1. System was kept at a temperature of 20 ¿C.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The existing system included mechanical pre-treatment (thick barrier, thin barrier, and rotational flow grit chamber) followed by an oxidation ditch reactor and a secondary sedimentation tank. Sludge from the mechanical pretreatment was sent to a landfill and sludge from the secondary sedimentation tank was recycled to the oxidation ditch reactor and sent to a plate and frame press followed by land application. A biological treatment system was inserted between the grit chamber and the oxidation ditch reactor. The biological system consisted of a regulating pond, hydrolytic acidification reactor, hydrolytic sedimentation tank, followed by two parallel moving bed bio reactors (MBBR).

Every pool has a square section of 240 m2 and a height of 7.2 m, providing a working volume of 1728 m3. The seeding sludge quantity (from the oxidation ditch) was adjusted to approximately 10 g/L mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS) for every hydrolysis/acidification pool.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater from the primary sedimentation tank was pumped into the aerobic granular sequencing batch reactor and passed through the sludge blanket. A bubble column with a diameter of 20 cm and working volume of 32 L was used as the aerobic granular sequencing batch reactor (SBR) and for the cultivation of aerobic granules. The membrane disk diffuser with the same cross section area was installed at the reactor bottom for air supply. The bubble column was operated sequentially with feeding, aeration, settling and discharging.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The membrane bioreactor (MBR) technology consisted of an activated sludge tank (90 L) and a filtration unit (30 L) for a total MBR volume of 120 L. The filtration unit contained a submerged ultrafiltration hollow fibre membrane module (0.93 m2 active area; 0.4um nominal pore size; PVDF membrane material). The MBR was operated in cycles of filtration and backwash. The permeate flow was controlled by a reversible pump.
