TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater is fed to the electrocoagulator from the bottom. The electrodes are positioned within the reactor vertically. The processed wastewater then overflows into a separation tank, where the reactions initiated in the electrocoagulator continue to occur and sludge begins to settle out of suspension. The pilot electrocoagulation system was within a modified 20 foot shipping container.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The coagulation unit can handle up to 10 m3/hr of flow, but typical highly polluted water is typically processed at a rate of 5 m3/hr. The volume of the reactor is 15-20 L (depending on electrode configuration/spacing). The retention time of the wastewater in the reactor is about 20 seconds.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION:
Low salinity wastewater flows to API separator and then an equalization tank. From there it enters a DAF system. After the DAF system, the wastewater enters the activated sludge system, which consists of aerobic biological reactors and final clarifiers. Some of the wastewater goes through tertiary treatment for solids removal (Actiflo) and blended with surface water and discharged to a water treatment plant. The remainder is blended with MBR permeate before discharge.
Brine is collected in a buffer tank, passes through heat exchangers, then through an API Separator and a DAF system. Prior to the API separator, low salinity wastewater is mixed with the brine. After the DAF system, the water is run through Nutshell filters designed to reduce O&G concentration. After the filters, the water is discharged into equalization tanks. There are two parallel trains with a hydraulic residence time of 12h. The equalization tank effluent is mixed with return sludge and flows to the anoxic reactors of the MBR treatment system. After the anoxic reactors, the wastewater travels to the aerobic reactors. The effluent is then split and is treated by 4 membrane trains. The permeate collects in a tank which, when it overflows, is directly discharged to the Paraiba do Sul River. The sludge is collected and returns to the head of the plant.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium hydroxide was dosed in the MBR to maintain pH.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Each membrane train consists of 3 GE ZeeWeed 500D membrane cassettes, which provides a total of 18,200 m2 of membrane surface area. The hydraulic retention time of the anoxic and aerobic reactors are 3.3h and 8.7h respectively.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The treatment process begins with oil removal via an API separator. H2O2 and FeCl2 are then injected for chemical oxidation. The wastewater then passes through Dissolved Nitrogen Flotation (DNF) units, then is collected in an equalization tank. From there, the wastewater goes through an activated sludge bioreactor then secondary clarification with recycled activated sludge. This is recycled back to the bioreactor and waste activated sludge to aerobic digestion, an aerated pond and polishing pond prior to direct discharge from their outfall.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Influent wastewater concentration of COD and sulfides varied significantly; as a result, H2O2 and FeCl2 dosing had to be constantly adjusted. However, H2O2 is applied to control DO in the inner track between 2-3 ppm with FeCL2 as a catalyst.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Wastewater is processed through the effluent plant at a rate of 2,500 gpm. The oxidation ditch has a detention time of 5.2 hours under average conditions of wastewater plus recycled activated sludge and fire water flows.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The pilot plant consisted of a coagulation tank with two rapid mixers (120 rpm), a flocculation tank with a slow mixer (30 rpm), and a lamella clarifier. The plant was fed with ozone column effluent.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Ferric chloride solution (40%) was added to the coagulation tank with dosages between 50 and 200 mgFe/L. Sodium hydroxide (25%) was also added for pH control. A cationic polymer was added in the flocculation tank (dosage 5 mg/L).
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The coagulation tank volume was 2 m3. The flocculation tank had a volume of 6 m3, and the lamella clarifier had a surface area of 10 m2. Ozone effluent was fed at a flow rate of 10 m3/h.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater from a refinery was used in the pilot unit. It was first processed through an API separator for oil removal, then passed through multi-media filters before being treated in an EcoRight MBR pilot unit. The pilot unit consists of a 6.83 m3 aeration tank, a 0.39 m3 membrane operating system tank, a 0.98 m3 filtrate storage tank and pumps, a blower and instrumentation and control system. Air is supplied to the aeration tank through coarse bubble diffusers.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Phosphoric acid was added to the aeration tank to supplement the phosphorus nutrient requirements.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The unit is capable of processing 10,900 liters of oily refinery wastewater per day. Volumes of the MBR aeration tank, membrane operating system tank, and filtrate storage tank were 6.83, 0.39, and 0.98 m3, respectively. System HRT and SRT was 8.7 hours and 20 days, respectively. A chiller was installed to maintain a temperature less than 35 degrees Celsius, to ensure nitrification. Aeration to the aeration tank was delivered via coarse bubble diffusers.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The pilot study used electrocoagulation unit effluent which was treated for 15 minutes. This was followed by screening (800 micron) and flocculation-flotation with the GEM system which is a hybrid centrifugal/DAF system. Coagulants were delivered directly into the flotation hydrocyclone unit.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Flocculants tested in the GEM system were C-498 HMW from KEMIRA at 55% charge and A-130 HMW from KEMIRA at 30% charge. Average doses were 30-40 ppm of anionic flocculant and 10 ppm of cationic flocculant.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: System HRT was 9 GPM/ft2.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The pilot system consisted of a anti-fouling membrane unit, a control panel, pumping skid, batch tank, CIP tank, and pretreatment strainers. Wastewater from the zinc smelting process was collected and then passed through PE strainers to avoid damage to the membranes. It was then gathered in a batch tank and passed through the ultrafiltration membranes.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Average flux recorded for the system was 162.9 LMH. System was operated at a pressure of 1.5 kg/cm2 for 8h a day. Membrane material was PES (150 kDa). Treatment capacity for the system was approximately 6.5 m3/hr.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater from painting and metal finishing processes is collected in six large plastic tanks. From there it is mixed and pumped to primary treatment EQ tank. After EQ, water is pumped to three smaller reaction tanks where pH is adjusted, first to around 10 for the best nickel removal with addition of FLOMIN polymeric dixanthate precipitant, followed by second tank where aluminum sulfate is added for phosphate removal and pH is reduced to around 8. The third tank is used to provide additional time for the precipitation reactions to fully occur. From the third tank water is pumped to the flocculation-flotation system - the Gas-Energy Mixing (GEM) System. The GEM system is a hybrid centrifugal hydrocyclone-DAF unit where high molecular weight cationic and anionic flocculants are added and solids are floated and removed.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: FLOMIN polymeric dixanthate precipitant, aluminum sulfate, high molecular weight cationic and anionic flocculants
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The Gas-Energy Mixing (GEM) System can operate at flows between 75 and 150 GPM.
MANUFACTURER: Clean Water Technology Inc. - GEM system

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION:
Wastewater from painting and metal finishing processes is collected in six large plastic tanks. From there it is mixed and pumped to primary treatment EQ tank. After EQ, water is pumped to three smaller reaction tanks where pH is adjusted, first to around 10 for the best nickel removal with addition of FLOMIN polymeric dixanthate precipitant, followed by second tank where aluminum sulfate is added for phosphate removal and pH is reduced to around 8. The third tank is used to provide additional time for the precipitation reactions to fully occur. From the third tank water is pumped to the flocculation-flotation system - the Gas-Energy Mixing (GEM) System. The GEM system is a hybrid centrifugal hydrocyclone-DAF unit where high molecular weight cationic and anionic flocculants are added and solids are floated and removed.
The pre-treated process wastewater is mixed with domestic sewage wastewater in an equalization tank and then supplied to a 200 gpm self-cleaning rotary drum screen. Wastewater is gravity fed from the screen to the 40,000 gallon EQ where it is then pumped to the 20,000 gallon anoxic tank for nitrogen removal. From the anoxic tank the wastewater gravity feeds (via piped connection in the wall of the anoxic tank) to the 8,800 gallons pre-aeration tank. In the pre-aeration tank activated sludge develops from nutrient consumption and oxygen supplied by blowers coupled with fine bubble diffusers located on the floor of the pre-aeration tank.
From the pre-aeration tank, wastewater gravity feeds to the two 8,800 gallon membrane tanks. The membranes in the membrane tank (Kubota flat sheet) pull the effluent and separate the water from the activated sludge. MBR effluent is either discharged to the POTW, or delivered to the RO feed tank for further treatment (for onsite reuse). The RO concentrate is discharged to the POTW.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: FLOMIN polymeric dixanthate precipitant, aluminum sulfate, high molecular weight cationic and anionic flocculants
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The Gas-Energy Mixing (GEM) System can operate at flows between 75 and 150 GPM. Pre-treated paint process and domestic wastewater are combined for a total design flow rate of 64,000 gallons per day flow to the MBR/RO system.
MANUFACTURER: Clean Water Technology Inc - GEM system; Kubota - MBR; Aeration tank blowers - Aerzen

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The pilot-scale plant contained an equalization tank, aerobic bioreactor (aeration tank), UF membrane, system, permeate holding tank, along with chemical addition (for nutrient feed and maintenance cleaning) pumps, feed pumps and air supply blowers. The pilot system was constructed with skid-mounted equipment installed at the coke by products plant. The waste water stream for the pilot feed was collected after passing through a spiral heat exchanger. A feed equalization tank was used by the pilot plant to provide a reservoir of 500 gallons of wastewater, which was pumped to the aerobic bioreactor at a flow rate ranging from 0.1 to 0.4 gpm (flow rate determined by the desired hydraulic retention time) using a peristaltic pump. The aerobic bioreactor operational volume was kept around 950 gallons. The mixed liquor feed pump (process pump), located near the bottom of the aerobic bioreactor, was used to feed the mixed liquor to the membrane tank. The membrane tank was equipped with a free overflow, allowing the mixed liquor to recycle back to the aeration tank. The ZeeWeed® UF pilot operated continuously, either discharging permeate to the 200 gallon permeate holding tank or recycling permeate back to the membrane tank. Sludge was wasted from the membrane tank and directed to the ammonia dike sump pit.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Nutrients (i.e. phosphoric acid) along with caustic soda and sulphuric acid for pH control were delivered to the aeration tank as needed.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: MBR’s aerobic suspended-growth environment is maintained in the bioreactor via diffused aeration and continuous mixing of the mixed liquor at concentrations of 10,000 mg/L. The aerobic bioreactor operational volume was kept around 950 gallons. The bioreactor design HRT was 86 hours. System SRT was maintained at 77 days by wasting approximately 15 gallons of sludge per day.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The pilot plant has a feeding system which includes a tank with a feeding pump and a filter element. The treatment group has two lines of membrane pressure vessels. In each line there are two membrane modules in series, with a total membrane filtration area of 24 m2 per line. Only one line was used for the study, with a total of four membranes sized 4"x40". Pretreatment of concentrate alkaline waters required to oxidize cyanides. Following pre-treatment, spiral wound type RO membranes with an effective membrane filtration area of 6 m2 were utilized.
MEDIA_TYPE: Fully aromatic polyamide advance composite membrane
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Feed volume was 2 m3/h, permeate flow was 1 m3/h and the test occurred over 8h. Three tests occurred: A continuous purge of the circuit without recirculating any stream. The feeding goes cross the system only once. The second test had some rejections come out of the system and some others mixed in the feed tank with the effluent. The tests are carried out with external recirculation. The final test recirculates the reject into the high pressure pump system with internal recirculation.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The solution flowing out from rinsing tank No. 1 has an initial concentration of: CuSO 4 .5H20: 50 g./1 (Cu = 12.7 g/l), H2SO 4 (97%): 10 g./1. The solution is stored into a holding tank T1 and from there is pumped by a centrifugal pump, at low pressure, through a cartridge filter (CF) to a positive displacement pump. This pump feeds a nanofiltration membrane at a pressure high enough to guarantee the production of 150 1/h permeate (initially 30 bar growing up to 65-70 bar all along with the increase of copper sulfate concentration in the brine). The membrane rejection remains unvaried beyond 99.9% so that the product looks like to a clean transparent, colourless solution with copper concentration of only few mg/l. The permeate on the first membrane is stored in a buffer tank and from there is pumped with the flow rate of 150 l/h in the last rinsing vat as demineralised makeup water. The concentrate, increasingly richer in copper sulfate content, is continuously recycled into the first holding tank, as long as necessary to reach the concentration equal or a little higher of that needed in the electroplating bath of about 60 g/l.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Feed 2 m3/h, 2 NF membranes DK4040F 1310, P 1 0.4 kW, P2 5.0 kW. The concentration cycle, i.e. the time necessary to take the concentration of the solution flowing from the first rinsing van to 60 g/l, is completed in about 42 h.
OANDM_COST:
The plant is kept working for about 10 h/d and runs without any attendance except for a very short flushing operation at the end of the daily operation.
Saves 15,000 Euros per year in make up of reagents.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The bench/pilot system consisted of a 200-gallon feed tank, a 50 gallon bioreactor, and a ZeeWeed® ultrafilter with a membrane surface area of 10 ft.2. In this system, an aerobic suspended-growth environment is maintained in the bioreactor via diffused aeration and continuous mixing of the liquor. The membranes are configured as small-diameter tubules, and are bundled in a cartridge for easy handling. The cartridge is suspended in the bioreactor. Effluent water passes concentrically into the membranes under a small vacuum induced by pumping versus under high pressure.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Phosphoric acid and ammonia were added to the bioreactor.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The bioreactor was operated at ambient temperature conditions, which averaged 55F and ranged from 50F to 70F. The D.O. ranged from 0.3 to 5.7 mg/L in the bioreactor and was regulated based on influent feed concentrations and rate of microbial activity. The pH remained in the range of 7.0 to 8.0 SU, and did not require a chemical adjustment. Overall, the organic loading rate (lb COD/day-1000 ft3 reactor volume) average 100, while the hydraulic residence time was maintained at 1.0 days as the mixed-liquor suspended solids level approached 8000 mg/L.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The pilot plant consisted of a primary clarifier and an MBR with an anoxic and an aerobic compartment for denitrification and nitrification, respectively. Submerged ultrafiltration flat sheet membrane plates (Huber MembraneClearBox, PP carrier, PES membrane, 7 m3, 15-30 L·m-2·h-1, 38 nm pore size, 150 kDa) were used. Wastewater from the aerobic compartment was recycled to the anoxic compartment (6-8 m3/day). The excess sludge amount accounted for 20-50 L/day. Water was sampled prior to entering the clarifier and after leaving the aerobic compartment.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The average influent flow rate was 1.2 m^3 of wastewater per day. The sludge concentration in the MBR was on average 2 g/L, the sludge age 30-50 days (organic sludge load 0.06-0.1 gCOD·gTSS- 1 · d- 1 corresponding to 0.03-0.05 gBOD5·gTSS-1·d-1), the average operating temperature was 29 °C (temperature of wastewater 27-28 °C), pH 7.8, and the conductivity 1100 µS/cm. Oxygen concentration in the aerobic compartment was maintained by aeration at 3 ± 2 mg/L.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION:
For the test run reported here (data from Table 1) The first was conducted to simulate a 60 gpm/ft2 overflow rate through the clarifier.
Raw influent was pumped to the treatment box at a rate of 175 gpm and mixed with 175 gpm of
effluent (simulating stormwater) returning from the clarifier. A total of 350 gpm was then
pretreated with 2 mg/l of sulfide, sufficient lime slurry to produce a process pH of 10.5, and
oxidized in an aeration chamber before being treated in the ballasted flocculation and clarification process.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Treatment box: In the primary neutralization chamber, hydrated lime slurry was added to raise the pH to 5.8.  In the aeration chamber, lime slurry was added to raise the pH to 10.5 and 2mg/L sulfide was also added. Ballasted Flocculation: In the maturation chamber, anionic polymer was added.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The clarifier overflow rate was 60 gpm/ft^2. The flow rate through the system was 350 gpm made up of 175gpm  raw influent and 175 gpm of clarifier effluent (simulating stormwater).

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The aerobic sludge digester component of the modified MBR system was designed to operate as follows; digester feeding to capacity, solids settling (approximately 4 to 5 hour period), supernatant removal and repetition of these steps until the digester solids no longer settle. The major components of the pilot plant were a 1.514 m^3 aerobic membrane bioreactor coupled to a UF membrane unit containing 1.95 m^2 of membrane area, operating in conjunction with a 1.514 m^3 aerobic sludge digester. Start-up of the aerobic sludge digester was initiated by adding 0.757 m^3 of waste solids from the aerobic bioreactor, 8 l of commercially available catalytic seed material, formulated specifically to promote TFOG oxidation, and make-up water to a total volume of 1.514 m^3. After batch operation for a period of 5 days, the sludge  digester contents were allowed to settle for a period of approximately 2 hours and then 0.606 m^3 of supernatant was decanted after which 0.352 m^3 of waste solids from the bioreactor were added. The cycle of batch operation, solids settling (i.e., quiescent conditions for a period of 4 to 5 hours), supernatant removal (if necessary to accommodate new feed solids) and bioreactor waste solids feeding, continued until the aerobic sludge digester solids no longer settled at which time a portion of the aerobic sludge digester contents were removed. Aerobic sludge digester solids were removed only 2 times during the 90 day period. The frequency of solids feeding was 2 to 3 times per week. Air was added to the sludge digester to maintain complete mixing and a dissolved  oxygen (DO) concentration greater than 2 mg/l. The sludge digester pH was not controlled and ranged from 6.5 to 8.0 during the study.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: HRT: 2.3 days; Temperature: 31°C; solids retention time (SRT): 28 days; MLTSS: 18.33 g/l; MBR bioreactor TFOG: 8575 g/l; membrane specific flux^2, 0.22 l/m^2h/kPa

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The GM Windsor full-scale MBR-aerobic digester system consists of a bioreactor 9.14 m in diameter by 12.2 m high and an aerobic sludge digester of equivalent dimensions. The bioreactor typically operates at a liquid height of approximately 10.1 m corresponding to a volume of 660 m^3. The bioreactor is coupled to parallel operating, UF membrane units. Each unit represents 732 m^2 of membrane area. Since start-up of the modified system, 1 to 3 membrane units have operated, the number dictated by the volume of wastewater to be treated and the efficiency of the membrane units. Aerobic sludge digester solids were removed (i.e., discharged off-site from the MBR-aerobic sludge digester system) 1 time during the 154 day operating period. That event (day 82 through 84) was prompted by the build-up of a significant layer of floating oily solids on the liquid surface of the aerobic sludge digester. It should be noted that on day 85, solids were also directly wasted off-site from the bioreactor.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Mean wastewater flow: 245 m^3/day; HRT: 2.76 days; MLVSS or MLVS: 37.5 g/l; COD volumetric load: 2.62 kg/m^3 day; Temperature: 22-36 degrees Celsius; Calculated SRT: 415 days; Yield (Yn): 0.08 g VSS or VS/g CODr; membrane flux: 58 l/m^2h

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Raw industrial electroplating wastewater is first sent to a mixing tank where liquid pineapple waste and sodium hydroxide are added for pH adjustment. The waste then gravitationally feeds the 0.2 m3 bioreactor. The bioreactor effluent then passes through flocculation and coagulation units. Sludge from the units is dried separately, while liquid effluent from the units is further treated through powdered activated carbon columns.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Mixing Tank: 1-20% Liquid Pineapple Waste (v/v), 12.5% Sodium Hydroxide (v/v); Flocculation: Alum (0.4-1.5 L); Coagulation: Anionic Polymer (0.4-2.0 L)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Bioreactor Flow: 0.11-0.33 m3/h; Bioreactor Carrier Material: Rubber Wood Sawdust

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The constructed wetland system (CWS) consists of four-stage down flow wetland cells. Each stage was configured using 10 cm of gravel followed by another 65 cm of the alum sludge cakes and 10 cm of gravel. The CWS was operated in tidal flow mode in which wastewater was periodically loaded and drained from each stage in batches and the loading and draining operations were controlled by pumps. Common reeds, Phragmites australis, were planted on top of each stage at the beginning of the experimental trials.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Hydraulic loading rate: 0.29 m3/m2d

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Tannery wastewater from a conventional secondary treatment system (activated sludge) was fed to a horizontal subsurface flow constructed wetland (CW) system, with an area of 72 m2 and a bed depth of 0.35 m, through a perforated polyvinylchloride (PVC) rigid pipe with a hydraulic flow control. TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The high- and low-concentration printed circuit board (PCB) industrial wastewaters were introduced to the electrochemical-coagulation (EC) reactor alternatively every 20 minutes over the course of the 80-minute operation time. The EC reactor was constructed from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) (capacity = 12 L) with aluminum electrodes (surface area = 0.3025 m2) that are arranged in a monopolar configuration.  The EC reactor also included a programmable logic controller (PLC) that was developed in-house to provide the optimal current signal according to the pre-measured conductivity value identified during the lab-scale tests.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The membrane bioreactor (MBR) consisted of laboratory pumps for feed flow and permeate suction, a blower with a diffuser placed under the hollow fiber membrane to prevent membrane fouling and mix the bioreactor, and a pressure gauge. The membrane was backflushed with effluent for 10 seconds every 9.75 minutes with the backflush rate 1.5 times bigger than the effluent flow rate in order to remove deposits on the membrane surface. The bioreactor was inoculated with activated sludge from a full-size municipal wastewater treatment plant with initial 10 g/L of mixed liquor suspended solids (MLSS) in the bioreactor. After a 38-day adaptation period when activated sludge was fed with tested real wastewater, the continuous treatment experiment was closely monitored during the next 22 days on the site of the wastewater discharge concurrently with the existing full scale treatment plant.
MEDIA_TYPE: Zenon ZeeWeeTM-10 hollow fiber membrane (vertically submerged)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Filter membrane pore size: 0.4 µm; Filter membrane surface area: 0.92 m2; Feed water flow rate: 5 L/h; Permeate flux: 5.43 L/m2h; Hydraulic retention time: 8 hr; Air flow: 6.5 m3/h

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Liquid-liquid extraction consists of a water purification phase, metal recovery stage, and a sulfate recovery phase. The water purification stage consisted of pumping the wastewater from a flooded mine shaft through a bag-type particulate filter to a set of five mixer-settler units (two-compartment tanks) that mix the wastewater with extractant (an unidentified organic liquid) to produce purified water and extractant loaded with metal and sulfate ions . The metal recovery stage consisted of the loaded extractant entering another set of mixer-settler tanks counter-clockwise with aqueous sulfuric acid solution to form an iron sulfate concentrate that is harvested for reuse.  The sulfate recovery stage consisted of the remaining loaded extractant entering another set of mixer-settler tanks counter-clockwise with an aqueous potassium carbonate solution to form a potassium sulfate concentrate that is also harvested for reuse.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system is an ADVENT Integral System (AIS), which is an activated sludge system with integrated clarification designed to achieve nitrification and denitrification. The system is an integrated unit that includes an anoxic stage, followed by an aerated stage with recycle to the anoxic stage, and a final clarifier, with sludge recycle to the anoxic stage .  The operational capacity of the system during these investigations was 900 gpm. There was no other information on operating parameters or design elements of the system.

The system was designed for a single AnoxKaldnes MBBR reactor to operate as pretreatment for existing activated sludge trains. The activated sludge trains (three in total) had a combination of two Infilco Type “S” Aero-Accelator activated sludge units with an integrated clarifier (2 trains operating in parallel) and a third standard activated sludge basin (South Biotreater) with a separate circular secondary clarifier. The aeration system is designed as a non-clogging aeration system with a 50% turndown capacity while still maintaining even distribution of air through the entire aeration system. Effluent from the secondary clarifiers flowed to sand filters and a chlorine contact basin prior to being discharged to surface waters.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: A chlorine contact basin was the final step in the process, but chlorine dosage was not described.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: MBBR parameters: 5.2 MGD average flow rate; 2.35 hour hydraulic retention time; Design maximum temperature of 104 degrees F; 85 ft diameter; 12 ft water depth; Wet volume of 68,042 cubic ft.
MANUFACTURER: AnoxKaldnes MBBR, Infilco Type S Aero-Accelator

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater was fed to two buffer tanks (13.2 m^3 each). A pump for each tank fed the biological treatment unit. The pilot plant was composed of three biological tanks in series giving approximately a 50/50 split of anoxic and aerobic volume: (1) an anoxic denitrification tank (2.3 m^3), (2) an aerated nitrification tank (0.8 m^3), and (3) an aerated membrane tank (1.4 m^3). The wastewater was fed to the denitrification tank of the pilot plant, where two mixers were installed to keep the activated sludge properly mixed. From the denitrification tank, the activated sludge passed to the nitrification tank through an opening in the bottom of the wall separating the two tanks. In the nitrification tank the activated sludge was aerated by a set of diffusers which also provided sludge mixing. From the nitrification tank the sludge was transferred to the membrane tank by a volumetric pump, from which return activated sludge (RAS) overflowed back to the denitrification tank. The membrane tank contained a module of Puron hollow-fiber membranes.
MEDIA_TYPE: Puron hollow-fiber membranes, model A 30 HS, PES material - Poly Ether Sulphone, nominal cut off at 0.02 µm
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: A 5% solution of sodium hydroxide was added to the nitrification tank to keep the pH between 7.1 and 7.7. Beginning July 1, acetic acid (10% solution) was added to the denitrification tank to complete denitrification. Ferric chloride (5% solution) was added to the membrane tank in November to precipitate phosphate and verify the effectiveness of this process. Beginning in September. spent caustic was added in the bottom of the denitrification tank at a flow rate equal to 0.1% of the wastewater flow rate. All chemicals were added through metering pumps whose flow rate was regulated manually.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The flow rate was 420 L/h; the average hydraulic retention time was 10.6 h. The flow rate was lowered in August due to membrane fouling (292 L/h) but was recovered by September after cleaning. Recycle from the membrane averaged 570% of incoming flow rate. There was a long solids retention time (SRT) of 35-45 days. Membrane was made of Poly Ether Sulphone material, nominal cut off at 0.02 µm.
MANUFACTURER: Mixer: BM Tecnologie Industriali, Italy, model GCC.11030.S.225/2; Membrane: Puron hollow-fiber membranes model A 30 HS supplied by Koch Membrane Systems

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: System will treat an average of 550 m3/d wastewater and a maximum of 700 m3/d. System includes the following components: Rotary drum screens, 2 balance tanks with mixers and pH control system, 2 biology tanks with fine bubble diffusers, membrane tanks including 88 Zenon ZW-500c membrane modules per tank, 2 permeate tanks, liquid oxygen tank and vaporizer, 2 ozone generators, ozone injection skid, ozone contactor, ozone degas vessel, atmospheric flash tank, effluent wet well, ozone destruction system, odor/off gas scrubber, flocculator reactor (for WAS), multipoint polymer feed system, disk thickener, thickened sludge storage tank, and a centrifuge. Ozone dosage control mechanism is flow based, but can also be controlled by the operator.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: ozone at various doses depending on the level of APIs. pH control system is included in the balance tanks; however, chemical additions are not specified.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Actual flow rate: 103 gpm average, 99 gpm min, 119 gpm max. design flow rates: 101 gpm avg flow; daily max: 128 gpm. Tank sizes: Balance - 220 m3; Biology - 220 m3; membrane - 27 m3; permeate - 7.6 m3; ozone contactor - 15 m3; ozone degas vessel - 15 m3 (working volume 1.8 m3); atmospheric flash - 0.9 m3; effluent wet well - 11.5 m3. Membrane surface area: 2,044 m2 per cassette. Ozone generators are capable of 13.6 kg/hr each.
MANUFACTURER: Membranes - Zenon Environmental ZW-500c; Ozone generators - WEDECO PDO 1000

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: This system treats hospital wastewater.  The system consists of an MBR, followed by ozonation, and can handle a max flow of 32 m3/hr. Ozone is introduced to the system via an injector or pump and then reacts in a 6 m3 reaction tank. Ozone is injected at a ratio of 1mg ozone/ 1mg DOC.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: ozone: 12.5 mg/L
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Max flow rate: 32 m3/hr. Ozone reaction time: 15 minutes. Ozone reaction tank size: 6 m3.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Pretreated BAPCO wastewater from the IAF unit is fed to 1-2 equalization tanks. The water is then pumped through cooling tanks prior to entering the MBR system. The MBR system was a two train systems each with 6 equal cells in series, 4 of which can operate either anaerobically or aerobically. During the performance test phase only one train was used. The first cell was anoxic, the next 4 cells were aerobic, and the last cell was anoxic. The cells were followed by 3 membrane tanks operating in parallel. The membrane tanks were aerobic. The treated effluent was discharged to the sea.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Acetic Acid and Urea (NaO4, dose: 70 l/h) were added to the biological cells. Spent caustic was added at a rate of 1 GPM (see Table 3 for details on caustic). Phosphoric acid was added in previous phases but it is not specified whether it is used in the performance test phase.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Average flow rate: 2,400 gpm. Each bioreactor cell has a volume of 550m3, with a total volume of 3300 m3 per train. Additionally there are membrane tanks with  volumes of 250m3. Biological cells average SRT: 30.50 days. Plant SRT: 23.5 to 37.5 days.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: This system treats the liquid organic wastes (LOW) waste stream from the semiconductor manufacturing facility and employs activated sludge and advanced oxidation processes. The system begins with a pre-anoxic treatment for degradation of organics, followed by treatment in an aerobic reactor for TMAH breakdown into ammonia. Then the waste stream goes through a clarifier followed by AOP where ammonia is oxidized to nitrate and finally a post anoxic treatment to denitrify the nitrate produced during AOP followed by a clarifier.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Concentrated HCl for pH adjustment.  The influent was blended with essential micro/macro nutrients (metals, alkalinity, and phosphorus) for proper microbial metabolism.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Volumes in L: Pre-anoxic - 0.7, Aerobic - 4.0, first Clarifier - 0.95, Post-anoxic - 0.4, second clarifier - 0.7. System was fed with LOW stream at 1:60 dilution.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Tetra-methyl ammonium hydroxide (TMAH) wastewater undergoes aerobic activated sludge treatment for TMAH breakdown into ammonia, after which it goes through a clarifier and then undergoes AOP to oxidize ammonia to nitrate. After this step the nitrate is denitrified via anoxic activated sludge and finally goes through another clarifier.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Concentrated HCl for pH adjustment.  The influent was blended with essential micro/macro nutrients (metals, alkalinity, and phosphorus) for proper microbial metabolism.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Sizes in L: Aerobic - 27, First clarifier - 15, Post-anoxic - 4, Second clarifier - 0.8. System received TMAH waste stream at 1:6 dilution.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: A dual sludge system (DSS) supplemented with PAC was used to treat herbicide production wastewater which has already gone through physico-chemical pretreatment at the existing full scale treatment plant. The first stage was a conventional activated sludge (CAS) system consisting of an equalization tank, microaerobic reactor, aerobic reactor and a secondary gravitational clarifier for biomass separation. The water then entered the second sludge system, an MBR system, which consisted of an aerobic reactor supplemented with PAC followed by a 65L post-anoxic reactor and a 36L membrane tank for final biomass separation. The membrane tank employed a ZW10™ submerged hollow fiber ultrafiltration polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membrane module. A reversible gear pump was used for backwashing.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Eq tank: 5 cm3/day  of phosphoric acid solution 79%w/w; MBR aerobic reactor: 600g of PAC (Shanxi Sincere SX000X) to reach an equilibrium concentration of 2000 mg/l; MBR post-anoxic reactor: 0.5L/h of diluted methanol solution 0.3%v/v.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow rate: 80 L/d. Treatment unit volumes: Eq tank - 150 L; CAS microaerobic reactor - 100 L; CAS aerobic reactor - 120 L; MBR aerobic reactor - 200L; MBR post-anoxic reactor - 65 L; membrane tank - 36 L. Influent pH - 7.7.
MANUFACTURER: Membrane module: GE Water; Backwash pump: Micropump

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The MBBR consists of 2 units in parallel operation, each with a volume of 601 m3 and operating water depth of 6.1 m. The MBBR consists of a tank equipped with an outlet sieve to retain the media, the media itself, and aeration/mixing. The aeration system utilizes a medium bubble design with stainless steel laterals and diffusers. The biofilm thickness is controlled by the movement of the media such that oxygen diffusion through the biofilm is encouraged. The MBBR uses AnoxKaldnes™ K3 media. Typical fill ratios range from 10-65% of the reactor volume. The MBBR effluent is discharged into a lagoon prior to discharge to the Saint Laurent River.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Influent Design Parameters: Flow (m3/d): Monthly avg = 9800; Daily max = 16350; Peak max = 27250; Temperature (degrees C): Monthly avg = 40; Daily max = 42. MBBR actual flow rate: 10193 m3/d. MBBR actual temperature: 23-52 (avg 40) degrees C. MBBR volume (each): 601 m3. MBBR operating water depth: 6.1 m. Media protected surface area: 500 m2/m3. Media specific gravity: 0.95 kg/dm3. Air supplied per unit: 2429 Nm3/hr. HRT at peak flow: 1 hr. HRT at min flow: 3 hrs.
MANUFACTURER: AnoxKaldnes™ K3 media used in MBBR

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The pilot scale DAF system for tertiary treatment treated clarified effluent from the full scale activated sludge biological treatment system. Effluent from the chlorine contact chamber was pumped to the pilot DAF skid. The DAF system included a chemical precipitation step, consisting of two mix tanks (flash mix and flocculation mix) and associated chemical feed components mounted on a skid . Coagulant was added in the flash mix tank, then a polymer flocculent was added in the flocculation mix tank. Wastewater then flowed into the DAF contact chamber where the floc made contact with micron-sized air bubbles, bringing the floc to the surface of the flotation cell where it was removed by a chain-and-flight skimmer system. Clarified effluent would pass under an internal baffle into the DAF clear well prior to discharge. Any solids that did not float would generally settle in the V-bottom of the DAF unit for discharge by periodic blow down.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Phosphate precipitation chemicals/coagulant (added to flash mix tank): Al2(SO4)3 (alum) and AlCl3; Average dose: 591 ppm. Flocculents (added to floc tank): 0.1-0.2% concentration cationic and anionic polymers; average dose: 0.85 ppm. pH control (added to flash mix tank): sodium hydroxide (NaOH)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Constant flow rate of 2.27 m3/hr (10 gpm). Flotation cell surface area: 0.28 m2. Hydraulic loading: 8.1 m3/hr/m2 of surface area.
MANUFACTURER: DAF: ETS Model RT-3 of 304SS construction

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The full-scale system was set up in the same way as the pilot scale: fine-screening, flow equalization, pretreatment dissolved air flotation (DAF), biological treatment (activated sludge), biological nutrient removal, tertiary DAF to remove TP, a sand filter, and ultraviolet disinfection. The tertiary DAF system consisted of two mix tanks (flash mix and flocculation mix) and associated chemical feed components mounted on a skid. Coagulant was added in the flash mix tank, then a polymer flocculent was added in the flocculation mix tank. Wastewater then flowed in to the DAF contact chamber where the floc made contact with micron-sized air bubbles, bringing the floc to the surface where it was removed by a chain-and-flight skimmer system.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: poly-aluminum chloride (coagulant) added to flash mix tank, dose: 450 ppm; anionic and cationic polymer added to floc tank, combined dose: 5.40 ppm
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Tertiary DAF design flow: 193 m3/hr; Average operating flow: 0.8 MGD; Flotation surface area: 22.30 m2; hydraulic loading: 8.66 m3/hr/m2; Flash mix tank HRT: 45 min; Floc tank HRT: 11 min; Float material collected in 8,000 gallon holding tank for decanting water prior to disposal

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater first passed through a bag filter, to remove large solids, then an oil/water separator to remove free oil. Wastewater then moved to an equalization tank before entering the ultrafiltration (UF) skid. The UF skid was made up of 8 ABCOR FEG 276 tubular membranes. After ultrafiltration the permeate went to a permeate storage tank.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: System was operated in a modified batch mode. Membrane length: 3m; Membrane diameter: 2.54 cm
MANUFACTURER: Membranes manufactured by Koch Membrane Systems. Equipment supplied and operated by EPS Wastewater LLC, Hebron, KY.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Process wastewater flows through two equalization tanks to an oil/water separator and into a bag filter. From there the wastewater is transferred to a UF working tank and then to an ultrafiltration skid before being discharged to the sanitary sewer.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: In-line chemical addition is shown on the process diagram; however, the specific chemicals and doses are not given.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The plant was originally desiged for a wastewater flow of 1000 m3 per day, but the facility wants to scale back the system design to 60 m3 per day.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater is collected in three equalization tanks (90 m3, 2 x 125 m3) and them pumped to an oil/water separator to remove free oil. Wastewater then flows through 75 micron bag filters for removal of larger solids that may damage the ultrafiltration (UF) membrane system.  The UF membrane system consists of a 70 m3 UF working tank and  8 horizontal spiral-wound cartridges (GE MW8040CF2071 membranes).
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Caustic 50% is added to UF working tank.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Oil/water separator design flow: 285 l/min. UF membrane design flow rate: 150 m3/day

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater flows through a 11 m3 process equalization tank, then through a bag filter. A Hollow fiber ultrafiltration unit is used to remove suspended and colloidal solids. The unit includes a working tank, bag filter, and UF skid. Lastly, wastewater is treated by chemical oxidation to remove color. Chemical oxidation step is a batch reactor.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Chemical oxidation: sodium hypochlorite
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: UF design flow rate: 27 m3/day

INDUSTRY: Organic chemicals, plastics and synthetic fibers
TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The first system (S1) is an anoxic-oxic tank made up of 5 different compartments and dimensions of 60m X 40m X 8m with an effective water depth of 7.2m. Two of the five compartments act as anoxic tanks (1st & 4th), while the other three are packed with polyurethane foams and are the contact oxidation tanks. In the anoxic tanks, agitators and vertical baffles were installed to avoid accumulation of suspended solids.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION:
Specialized refractory organic-targeting bacteria mainly consisting of Pseudomonas, Bacillus, Acinetobacter,
Flavobacterium and Micrococcus was introduced. Necessary organic substrates and inorganic
trace elements were added to stimulate the growth of these microorganisms.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The A/O tank had a size of 60 m x 40 m x 8m (L x W x H) and the effective depth of water was 7.2 m. The temperature of the wastewater during the upgrading phase was 27–32 C. Flow rate: 700 m3/d. Flow rate was varied to 800, 1200, and 1500 m3/d during the shock loading testing. HRTs corresponding to these flow rates are 21.6, 14.44, 11.52 h respectively.

INDUSTRY: Organic chemicals, plastics and synthetic fibers
TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The second system (S2) is an anoxic-oxic tank made up of 5 different compartments and dimensions of 60m X 40m X 8m with an effective water depth of 7.2m. Two of the five compartments (1st and 4th) act as anoxic tanks, while the  other three are the aeration tanks. In the anoxic tanks, agitators and vertical baffles were installed to avoid accumulation of suspended solids. S2 was operated in parallel to S1, under the same effluent and environmental conditions but without bioaugmentation (no polyurethane foams in the aeration tanks).
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The A/O tank had a size of 60 m x 40 m x 8m (L x W x H) and the effective depth of water was 7.2 m. The temperature of the wastewater during the upgrading phase was 27–32 C. Flow rate: 700 m3/d. Flow rate was varied to 800, 1200, and 1500 m3/d during the shock loading testing. HRTs corresponding to these flow rates are 21.6, 14.44, 11.52 h respectively.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Immersed MBR pilot system using ZeeWeed ultrafiltration membrane modules. The ZeeWeed membrane modules  are immersed in the membrane tank and wastewater is pumped into them, creating a small vacuum. Every 10 to 12 minutes the process pump backpulses permeate back into the bioreactor to prevent fouling. Airflow cleans the outside of the membrane fibers.

The WWTP consists of preliminary treatment for oil/tar removal and the biological treatment system for treatment of excess flushing liquor (waste ammonia liquor), wastewater from coke oven gas desulfurization, by-product wastewater (from light oil recovery), and some site stormwater. The ammonia still effluent is discharged to the equalization tanks. From here, the wastewater is cooled via spiral heat exchanges to <85 degrees Fahrenheit and an oil coalescer for free oil removal to mitigate membrane fouling. Nutrient augmentation for maintaining effective biodegradation in the MBR is supplied via phosphoric acid addition. Sludge dewatering for maintaining effective MLSS concentration in the bioreactor is provided with a belt filter press. These filter cakes solids are beneficially recycled to the coke ovens with the coal. Effluent following MBR treatment is collected, sampled, and pumped to the Monongahela River.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Phosphoric acid, caustic soda to maintain effective pH in the bioreactor.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The wastewater is cooled with a wet surface air cooler before flowing into a 225,000 gallon equalization tank equipped with jet mixing. From there wastewater goes into the coagulation mix tank where ferric sulfate is added. Subsequently, wastewater goes into the flocculant mix tank where polymer is added. From there, the wastewater goes into the mercury dissolved air flotation system. Effluent from the mercury DAF is pumped into the aeration basin feed tank where phosphoric acid, caustic and defoamer are added. From there, wastewater is pumped into the 875,000 gallon aeration basin. Finally, an additional DAF is used for clarification. Treated wastewater is discharged to DWSD.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: 375 ppm ferric sulfate, 12 ppm high cationic charged polymer. 0.01 gpm of phosphoric acid, 0.16 gpm of caustic, and 0.004 gpm of defoamer.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow rate into the WWTP is 200 gpm.

INDUSTRY: Canned and preserved fruits and vegetables processing
TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Fruit processing wastewater was delivered in a tote bin to the vinegar plant and a submersible pump transferred the wastewater to a 379 L feed tank equipped with a mixer. Nutrients were added and pH was adjusted by chemical addition in the tote bin or feed tank. A variable speed pump fed the wastewater from the feed tank through a flow totalizer to the bioreactor. The 568 L aerobic bioreactor tank is equipped with a GE Zee Weed 10 membrane module fitted with hollow fibers with 0.93 m2 of membrane area. A dedicated blower provides air scouring of the membranes as necessary. Membrane cleaning chemicals and metering pumps provided periodic cleaning of the membranes as needed. Effluent was pumped to a 19 L permeate/backpulse tank with an overflow to the floor of the plant.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Nutrients were added and pH was adjusted via chemical addition.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The pilot system could treat 151 liters per day.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: This membrane system is the same as the previous system, except that the nanofiltration membrane system has been replaced with a RO unit. Nickel sulfate makeup dropped from 220 kg/week to 10-15 kg/week, nickel chlorate makeup dropped from 50-60 kg/week to 5-7 kg/week, and boric acid makeup dropped from 40 kg/week to 2 kg/week.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Rejection rate of the membrane is 99.8% for nickel salts and 95% for boric acid. There is a constant permeate flow rate of 50-60 l/h, flowing directly into the last rinsing tank.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The experiments done with S. cerevisiae at a pilot scale were carried out utilizing a filter press, which consisted of a stack of 40 cardboard filters (2 µm porosity) interspersed with separators and pressed with a screw, and a rotary electropump capable to generate a flow of 200 L h-1. In order to load the cardboard filters with the yeast, 180 g of lyophilized biomass of S. cerevisiae strain Z were rehydrated in 15 L of deionized water and then flushed through the filter press until the cells were completely trapped inside the filters. Afterward, 15 L of 0.3% HCl water solution was circulated through the filter press for 30 min, followed by a flush of 15 L of deionized water for 1 h, in order to remove the acid solution. After the acid pretreatment, 15 L of diluted wastewater, at a Cr(VI) concentration of 390 mg/L, was flushed for 57 hours through the filter press.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: 15 L of 0.3% HCl water solution circulated through the filter press for 30 min as a pretreatment step

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: This system is a moving bed sand filter. Wastewater is pumped through the Astrasand filter and purified. The effluent that is discharged comes directly off the sand filter. The contaminated wash water, containing the metal-loaded biomass, is drained to a lamella separator or settling tank (for sludge thickening). The water, coming from the thickener, is recycled back into the sand filter. The sludge coming from the thickener is treated further in a filter press or a decanting centrifuge after addition of lime or flocculants, respectively. The filter cake obtained in this way, containing the metals, is recycled in a pyrometallurgical treatment facility (shaft furnace) of a nonferrous company.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Lime, Flocculants. The heavy metal-resistant and bioprecipitating Ralstonia eutropha CH34 (former name Alcaligenes eutrophus) was used together with the metal biosorbing bacteria Pseudomonas mendocina AS302 and Arthrobacter sp. BP7/26. An inoculum (20 L of each culture) of the three strains was prepared in Luria Broth medium. The final concentration of the bacteria in the sand filter water was approximately 10^8 cfu/ml.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS:
Wastewater from a nonferrous company was used after a neutralisation and precipitation step. This residual water contained 1.5 mg Co/L, 0.7 mg Ni/L, 0.2 mg Zn/L and 0.1 mg Cu/L, all analyzed by ICP. The COD was nearly 20 mg O2/L, and very low concentrations of nitrates (0.9 mg NO3–N/L), ammonia (0.5 mg NH4–N/L) or phosphates ( < 0.05 mg PO4–P/L) were present (as analyzed by standard methods). The input oxygen concentration was,
depending on the weather conditions, between 0 and 6 mg O2/L.  The Astrasand moving bed sand filter AS-30-40 with a diameter of 3.00 m, a filter bed height of 4.00 m and a filter bed volume of 12 m3 were filled with quartz sand with a grain -size diameter between 1.2 and 2.0 mm. The normal filtration velocity was between 6 and 7 m/h, and a feed flow between 20 and 45 m3/h was applied. The wash water flow was between 3 and 5 m3/h and the sand circulation speed was between 0.5 and 1.0 cm/min. The empty bed contact time was about 36 min.
MANUFACTURER: Astraco Water Engineering-Paques, Balk, The Netherlands

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system consists of a column slurry pilot reactor (PR). This is an acrylic cylindrical recipient with a volume of 15 L. The UV lamp (low pressure mercury lamp, 36 W at 253.7 nm) possesses a light intensity of 7 × 10-7 einstein/s and is protected by a quartz jacket, placed along the axis of the reactor. Air from a porous plate placed at the bottom of the reactor was bubbled to keep particles in suspension. Sieve plates were placed along the reactor in order to keep a uniform size of bubbles. For the pilot reactor, the TiO2 concentration was 1500 ppm and HuAs was 15 ppm.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Photocatalyst: P25 titanium dioxide to obtain concentration of 1500 ppm TiO2.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The CrVI removal efficiency was determined by measuring the CrVI in the supernatant following passage through the adsorptive media. The yellow CrVI-LDH sludge was centrifuged, washed and finally dried. Dried CrVI-LDH was mixed with water by the ratio of 1 g solid per 5 mL water and then transferred into a cylindrical stainless steel vessel with continuous stirring. The stainless steel vessel was sealed and filled with CO2 under the pressure of 2.5 Mpa for 14 h. The supernatant containing concentrated CrVI was then separated for CrVI determination and reuse. The sediment was rinsed with distilled water 3 times to determine the amount of residual CrVI.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Cl-LDH (320 g) was added into the wastewater under continuous stirring for 5 h for a dosage of 16 g/L
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 20 L CrVI-containing electroplating wastewater was used for the pilot-scale experiment. The CrVI concentration was 1031 mg/L and the pH of the wastewater was about 4.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater was stored in an initial storage tank, and then moved to a pH control tank (pH 2) where 2-3% sulfuric acid is added.  The wastewater then moves to the biological oxidation tank, where bacterial growth to oxidize ferrous to ferric ion occurs on a packed bed of polyurethane foam.  Ferric ion precipitation occurs in a tank (pH 4) where 10 M sodium hydroxide is added, and the wastewater is ultimately transferred to a settling tank where ferric hydroxide precipitates are removed.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: 2-3% H2SO4 and 10 M NaOH.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The bioreactor has an treatment volume of 100 liters.  Optimal HRT was 1 hour.
OANDM_COST: Process may not be cheaper than conventional processes.  Additional cost recovery possible from reuse of recovered materials and reduction in sludge volume.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: System consists of an aerated equalization tank followed by the Astrasand moving-bed filter. Water flows upward through the sand bed in a cylindrical vessel. The filtrate is discharged in the upper part of the filter. The filter bed is continuously moving downward and dirty sand is abstracted from the bottom, washed, and released back to the top of the bed. The sand circulation is based on the airlift principle. A lamella separator is used to separate the metal laden flocs from the wash water. The wash water is combined with the filtrate and sent to the sewer. Bag filters are used to dehydrate the settled sludge, with the bag filtrate also sent to the sewer.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Acetate as a carbon source (10.4 mg C/L) and nitrate as an electron acceptor (3.7 mg N/L) to supplement available oxygen in the feed.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The designed surface loading rate of the unit is 1.7-13 m/h and the feed flow rate is 1-8 m3/h. Acetate was the substrate of choice.
OANDM_COST: Cost calculations comprising all investment and operational costs demonstrated that comparable conventional water treatment techniques like precipitation with filtration, reverse osmosis or ion exchange are 50% to 100% more expensive that the patented MER

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION:
The combined rinse water of a flow rate of 20 m3/h from plating lines at the plant was collected in the rinse collection
sump, of which 2.0-2.2 m3/h of combined rinse water was transferred from the rinse collection sump to the pH adjustment sump for the pilot study. The remaining combined rinse water was pumped to the wastewater treatment plant (WWTP). A compressed air pipe with diffuser holes was installed at the bottom of the sump for well mixing during pH adjustment. The wastewater after pH adjustment overflowed into the raw feed water sump. The large suspended solids were partially removed by gravitational settling. The test feed water was then pumped to the pilot plant on the mezzanine floor. The suspended
solids above 50 um in the stream were further removed using a multi-media filter, and the filtrate was collected in the feed tank of the UF unit. The filtrate water was pumped through a 50-pm bag filter and then fed to UF membrane
modules where smaller suspended solids and colloidal materials were removed. The concentrated stream from the UF unit was drained to the WWTP. The UF permeate water was sent to the RO feed tank and then pumped to the RO unit for
removing dissolved solids. An ultraviolet (UV) unit and 5-um cartridge filters were installed prior to RO membranes to protect them from bacteria growing and foreign materials which may fall and trap inside the RO feed tank, respectively. The concentrate stream from the RO unit was partially returned to the RO feed line before the cartridge filters and partially bled to the WWTP. All RO permeate from individual pressure vessels was combined in one common
permeate line and sent to the product tank. The reclaimed water was pumped to one of the plating lines for reuse.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: NaOH dosing to raise pH from 1.9-3.2 to 5.5-7.6. A caustic solution was dosed to the permeate line to maintain the pH value of the reclaimed water in the range of 5.5 to 7.6.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 2.0-2.2 m3/h used for the pilot study.
MANUFACTURER: The UF unit contained four HF66-45-XMSOP modules from Koch Membrane Systems. Each pressure vessel held two ESPAl-4040 spiral-wound modules made of thin-film polyamide composite membranes by Hydranautics.
OANDM_COST: $68,300; labor assumed to be approximately 2 hr/day.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: A variable speed pump pumps solvent cleaner and spent solvent cleaning rinses from the feed tank to the membrane module. The permeate is recycled back into the feed tank. The membrane module contains three types of PAN hollow-fiber UF membranes.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The system was operated at a pressure of 0.1 MPa and a cross-flow velocity of 0.8 m s-1.
MANUFACTURER: Membrane manufacturers were Asahi Chemical, Japan and Motian Membrane Eng., China.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Feed stream for this system is a 20:1 ratio mixture of permeates of ultrafiltration of boron- and ethanolamine-containing coolants (used as a carbon source) and wastewater from electrochemical deburring processes. Wastewater was continually pumped into a completely mixed influent basin. From there it was treated through 7 fixed bed reactors. The influent basin and first two fixed bed reactors are operated under anoxic conditions, while the following five are aerated.  Biofilm is formed on polyethylene/clay sinterlamellas, manufactured by PELIA. Chemical oxidation of wastewater components was achieved with UV-activated H2O2 in a reactor equipped with a 150 W  mercury lamp.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Influent basin has a working volume of 1.13 m3, and each reactor has a working volume of 1.13 m3 and a liquid volume of 0.8 m3.  Polyethylene/clay sinterlamellas had a total surface area of 150 m2/reactor. Wastewater was recycled from the final reactor to the influent basin at a rate of 40 m3/day. UV-H2O2 conducted in a 300 ml reactor equipped with a 150 W mercury lamp.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Feed stream for this system is a 20:1 ratio mixture of permeates of ultrafiltration of boron- and ethanolamine-containing coolants (used as a carbon source) and wastewater from electrochemical deburring processes, "diluted" four-fold with another, less polluted industrial wastewater stream from spray-painting, surface phosphating, industrial washing machines, off-gas-purification, etc. Wastewater was continually pumped into a completely mixed influent basin. From there it was treated through 4 fixed bed reactors. The influent basin and first fixed bed reactors are operated under anoxic conditions, while the following three are aerated; fixed-bed reactors 5-7 were not required.  Biofilm is formed on polyethylene/clay sinterlamellas, manufactured by PELIA. Chemical oxidation of wastewater components was achieved with UV-activated H2O2 in a reactor equipped with a 150 W  mercury lamp.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Influent basin has a working volume of 1.13 m3, and each reactor has a working volume of 1.13 m3 and a liquid volume of 0.8 m3.  Polyethylene/clay sinterlamellas had a total surface area of 150 m2/reactor. Wastewater was recycled from the final reactor to the influent basin at a rate of 40 m3/day. UV-H2O2 conducted in a 300 ml reactor equipped with a 150 W mercury lamp.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The waste emulsion is pretreated via proprietary procedure, and is then passed through a metal sift to remove large particles. The feed tank is specially designed to separate the large oil droplets during the filtration operation. It has two separated parts with a connecting tube at the bottom. The large oil droplets float to the surface of the first part and are collected. The feed is then pumped to the tubular side of zirconia membrane modules. The permeate was bled off the unit as the retentate was recycled into the feed tank.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The mean flux of the membrane is 80 l/m2h. The mean pore size is 0.1-0.2 um. The membrane area is 0.22m3.
MANUFACTURER: Jiangsu Jiuwu High Technology Co Ltd
OANDM_COST: The price of the inorganic membranes used in this paper is cheaper than that of the imported polymeric membranes used at another steel plant.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The system consisted of four main treatment phases.  The first was to segregate the final rinse water from other more concentrated rinse waters used in plant processes and collect it. The second was to accomplish pre-treatment, using a combination of gravity settling, multimedia, bag, and cartridge filters to remove suspended solids and UV treatment to remove microorganisms.  A granular activated carbon column was used to remove organic contaminants and free chlorine. The carbon column is followed by cartridge filters to remove any entrained carbon particulates. Pretreated wastewater is then held in a filtrate buffer tank. From the filtrate buffer tank, wastewater undergoes final pretreatment via cartridge filters and UV, and then heavy metals were removed using a nanofiltration membrane system with a 2:1 membrane configuration (two pressure vessels in parallel, followed by one pressure vessel in series). Each pressure vessel had four NF membrane modules.  The NF concentrate stream could be recirculated to the gravity settler, and ultimately transferred to a conventional wastewater treatment system prior to discharge to sewer.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Dosing and chemical type were not specified, although chemical addition was indicated in cost section.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The operating treatment system capacity is 1.8 m3/h. Flowrate is 30 l/min.
OANDM_COST: Obtained design data for a full scale plant with capacity of 25 m3/hr. Expected payback period is 13 months.

CHEMICAL_ADDITION: HCl was used to control NH3 in the spent etchant.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Water flow ranged from 10-48 m3/h.
