TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater was pumped via peristaltic pump into a PVC column packed with 150 polyester fiber balls for filtration. The water then flowed through an spiral-wound ultrafiltration membrane cartridge. To minimize the fouling of the UF membrane, intense aeration, intermittent effluent discharge (15 min ON/1 min OFF), and continuous NaOCl (12%) and citric acid (50%) dosing was used. The water then flowed through a spiral-would polyamide reverse osmosis membrane (LFC1 4040). Each unit consisted of a high-pressure feed pump, pressure vessel, and a recirculation loop with a pressure gage and a flow meter.  This system was operated in continuous-feed mode with a recycle of concentrate flow to maintain the minimum concentrate flow requirements. Flows and pressures were controlled by adjusting the  feed, recycle, concentrate, and permeate valves.
MEDIA_TYPE: Filtration: polyester fiber balls; UF: spiral-would polyethersulfone membrane; RO:  spiral-would polyamide membrane
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: To minimized UF membrane fouling, continuous NaOCl (12%) and citric acid (50%) dosing was used (in addition to other processes).
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS:
PVC column - 130 cm tall, 115 cm packing height, 15 cm inside diameter. Fiber ball diameter - 2.5 cm. In this study,
the applied filtration velocities and flow pressures varied from 60 to 100 mhr-1 and 0.01 to 2.0 kgfsq-cm-1, respectively. The applied flow rate was approximately 144 m3hr-1 UF membrane cartridge dimensions: 5 cm (D)×15 cm (L), effective membrane filtration area: 10 m2, permeate flux: 26 Lm2min-1, operating pressure: 3.06 kgfsq-cm-1. RO membrane: effective membrane filtration area: 7.9 m2, desalination rate=99%, water production=2300 GPD 8.7 m3 d-1, permeate flux 0.18 m3m2h-1 (13 GFD) with 75% recovery.
MANUFACTURER: Peristaltic pump: Cole Parmer MasterFlex L/S®; Fiber balls: Tsinghua Tongang Co., Beijing, China; UF membrane: Fluid Systems, MI, USA; RO membrane: LFC1 4040 by Hydranautics Membrane Systems, CA, USA

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: A sulfide precipitation process is added to an existing lime precipitation wastewater treatment plant for treating underground mine drainage from a zinc mine. The contaminated water enters a contactor where H2S gas produced onsite in a bioreactor, is introduced for sulfide precipitation. The water then enters a clarifier. This process produces a saleable zinc concentrate containing copper, lead, and cadmium. The water then flows into the plant's existing lime reactor where lime is added for precipitation prior to another clarifier.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Thioteq technology (bioreactor): H2S gas generated in bioreactor onsite and fed to sulfide precipitation contactor. Lime reactor: 495 ton/yr lime.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design flow rate for sulfide precipitation contactor: 700 m3/d; Sludge volume: 31,000 m3/yr. The rate of sulfide generation in the bioreactor ranged from 0.26 to 0.43 kg sulfide/m3 acid mine drainage.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: An existing wastewater treatment plant was retrofitted by adding a struvite precipitation process. After the existing equalization tank, water entered the chemical mix tank where MgCl2·6H2O as an alternate source of magnesium ion was added to reach at 1:1:1 in the molar ratio of NH4–N:Mg:PO4–P for struvite formation and  then, the pH adjustment of the wastewater to 9 was achieved by the continuous addition of 5N NaOH. The liquid stream then moved to the struvite reaction tank where struvite was formed.  The solution was allowed to settle in the intermediate settler. The settled sludge was recycled to the chemical mixing tank in order to provide seeding material. The water then continued into the rest of the existing system, which included a fluoride removal tank, where fluoride was precipitated with CaF2 by adding CaCO3.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Chemical mix tank: MgCl2·6H2O as magnesium source (at a 1:1:1 molar ratio), 5N NaOH added continuously to adjust pH to 9. CaCO3 was added to final settler to precipitate fluoride.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Influent flow rate to existing plant: 500 m3/d. The mixing speeds in both of the chemical mixing tank and the struvite reaction tank were 250 rpm. Sludge recycle rate: 250m3/d. Sludge recycle suspended solids concentration: 10000 mg/L. Chemical mixing tank: volume (m3): 12, Contact time (h): 0.6; Struvite reaction tank: volume (m3): 12, Contact time (h): 0.6; Intermediate settler: volume (m3): 250, contact time (h): 1.2.
OANDM_COST: $996 US/d for magnesium and NaOH

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The wastewater enters an equalization basin, then flows to an aerobic tank, followed by an anoxic tank and another aerobic tank before going into the MBR. The wastewater goes through ultrafiltration before discharge.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Average biomass concentration of 6,500 mgVSS/L

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Truck cleaning wastewater enters the equalization tank and then enters the membrane bioreactor aerated with high purity oxygen. Oxygenation is carried out using a mechanically agitated contacting system called the In-Situ Oxygenation (I-SO™ aerator) developed by Praxair, Inc. Inflow is highly variable. An oxic/anoxic cycling strategy was implemented at in constant cycle intervals of 160 min ON, 45 min OFF.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: High purity oxygen for aeration
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The plant treats 50-100 m3/day of flow discontinuously in a 500 m3 volume reactor. Membrane pore size: 300 kD. An Equalization Tank stores the produced wastewater and feeds the MBR for about 10 hours during working days.
MANUFACTURER: Aerator - In-Situ Oxygenation aerator developed by Praxair, Inc.; Membranes - Orelis; Ammonia & Nitrate probe - Hach Lange

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The wastewater enters dual influent storage and equalization feed tanks, used alternatively in a batch mode. The water then enters the MBR -  an aeration basin equipped with submerged hollow fiber Zenon membrane modules. The treated water is directed alternatively to two effluent storage tanks. The final effluent is discharged batch-wise from the off-line tank after confirming it is of acceptable quality. The treated water is discharged by sewer to a POTW. The primary objective of the treatment system is removal of ammonia and VOCs.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Due to the high strength of the wastewater (design TOC of 14 000 mg/L, typical TKN of approximately 1 000 mg/L), the hydraulic retention time (HRT) in the MBR averages 20 days. Low membrane low design flux rate of 4.5 L/m2/h. Operating under high TDS (>20,000 mg/L) and MLSS (~40,000 mg/L).

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: System treats leachate from municipal landfill. Wastewater enters an equalization tank and then goes to an MBR. The MBR comprises an anoxic tank followed by two aerobic reactors (operating in parallel), then two batteries of cross-flow ultrafiltration membranes. Water is recirculated in the tanks by 20 HP tank recirculation pumps. The water is pumped from the aerobic reactors to the ultrafiltration membranes at a high rate (more than 15 times the forward flow) by high-pressure recirculation pumps (50 HP). Sludge is recycled from the membranes to the anoxic tank and aerobic tanks. Extensive flow equalization and off-line storage facilities are also provided to accommodate highly variable, rain-driven leachate generation rates.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Antifoaming agent addition and ferric dosing were used to correct start up problems with foaming and color, respectively.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow rate: 35,000 gpd. Plant operated in high temperatures (80-108 degrees F) and high MLSS (typically ~15,000 mg/L, up to 30,000 mg/L).

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The conventional activated sludge plant with a large secondary clarifier treats metallurgical coke manufacturing wastewater. It operates with an F/M ratio of 0.27/day, which is higher than recommended (0.13/day). It operates with a sludge blanket close to the clarifier weir, a well-settling, non-bulking sludge, and a low clarifier overflow rate  which allowed the plant to operate with record-breaking MLSS and MLVSS concentrations of up to 10,000 and 9 000 mg/L, respectively. System is designed to treat ammonia, phenol, and thiocyante rich wastewater.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Jar tests were performed regarding polymer (Zetag 7563) addition but the paper does not state that polymer was added to the system.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Clarifier surface overflow rate: 0.47 m/h. Clarifier solids loading rate: 7.7 kg/m2/h

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Pharmaceutical wastewater first enters a biological reactor where high purity oxygen is added by the I-SO floating mixing and oxygenation system. The oxygenator has a downward-pumping impeller within a draft tube that pumps oxygen deep within the basin and a hood that captures and promotes recirculation of bubbles. The water is then treated by two trains of external 0.15 µm ceramic cross-flow ceramic membranes, each with two banks of membranes in series. The leading set of membranes is high pressure and the trailing set is low pressure. DO was varied between 1.5 and 5.5 mg/L to assess the impact of DO on membrane fouling rates.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: High purity oxygen is added to the biological reactor (>99.5% O2 v/v)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Net flow: 4 m3/hr. The total available membrane surface area is about 220 m2. A nominal membrane flux of about 15-20 LMH is maintained in the system. DO and MLSS levels were varied. COD influent load was approximately 16,000 mg/L.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Textile wastewater first entered a biological reactor where high purity oxygen was added by a Mixflo side-stream mechanical oxygenator. Mixed liquor is withdrawn from the basin, mixed with oxygen and passed through a length of piping to increase the contact time and improve oxygen dissolution before being injected back into the basin. The water was then treated by immersed 0.03 µm hollow fiber membranes. DO was varied at 2, 6, and 10 mg/L to assess the impact of DO on membrane fouling.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: High purity oxygen was added to the biological reactor by the Mixflo side-stream mechanical oxygenator (>99.5% O2 v/v).
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow rate: 0.26 m3/hr. Membrane surface area is 37 m2. DO and MLSS were varied. Nominal flux of 11-12 LMH was maintained.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION:
The system starts with two API water/oil separator. Wastewater then went through benzene strippers to reduce the amount of benzene that went through the DAF system. Wastewater was then treated by chemical precipitation (adding coagulants and flocculants) then went through a DAF and then was discharged to a POTW. During upset conditions, wastewater could be sent to a diversion tank and be reprocessed prior to discharge. An automated system for chemical addition was installed in the DAF to improve effluent quality. 3D TRASAR measured turbidity and controlled chemical dosing for the system saving manpower and improving effluent quality of water discharged to the POTW. API water/oil separator and DAF sludge was treated by a 3 phase centrifuge system. The centrifuge removed much of the oil and solids returning
relatively clean wastewater to the treatment system. Recovered oil was reclaimed and solids
were further processed offsite.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: flocculants, coagulants (added in coagulant mix tank prior to DAF), acid/caustic. Automation technology, 3D TRASAR Technology for DAF (3DTfDAF), was used to control dosage using real time measurements of turbidity and pH.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: total flow rate of the system was 1,675 gpm. API water/oil separator capacity: 600 gpm each. DAF capacity: (00 gpm.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION:
Anaerobically-pretreated pulp and paper wastewater enters the IMBR (industrial MBR) system The MBR system consists of 2 bioreactors with ultrafiltration membranes in the center. Each MBR has 3 zones with mixed liquor recirculation from the 2nd zone, back to the 1st.  Mixed liquor recirculation capacity of up to five times the average influent flow is provided, but a recirculation flow approximately three times the influent  flow was generally used. All bioreactors have fine membrane disc diffusers. H2SOX (controlled H2S oxidation to elemental sulfur) operation of the industrial MBRs is initiated by restricting oxygen input to zone 1 of the bioreactor while maintaining DO concentrations of 1.0 and 1.5 in
zones 2 and 3. The IMBRs are served by eight membrane cell. Effluent from zone 3 from each bioreactor is combined and flows by gravity to the membranes. Recirculation flow back to the IMBR is pumped. Effluent is discharge to the regional outfall sewer.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Phosphoric acid was added throughout as a supplemental nutrient. Sulfuric acid is added to the bioreactor to maintain the bioreactor pH at values sufficient to avoid calcium carbonate precipitation, which was observed during pilot testing (GWF, 2009), and which might damage the membranes.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The volume of each bioreactor is 3,068 m3, for a total IMBR volume of 6,136 m3, providing a hydraulic residence time of 8.1 hours at the design average flow of 18.2 MLD. Membranes: Four cells are equipped with 12 Siemens Memcor membranes modules, with 7,220 m2 of membrane surface  area per cell, and four cells are equipped with 15 racks having 9024 m2 of membrane surface area per cell, giving a gross membrane flux of 11.7 L/m2-hr at the design average flow. The distribution of volumes between the three zones of 27.7, 48.0. and 24.3 percent for zones 1 through 3 was selected to accommodate biological nutrient removal in the companion municipal bioreactors and was maintained in the IMBRs. All zones of the IMBR are aerated, as discussed below. The aspect ratio (length-to-width ratio) of the three zones is 7.8, 2.9, and 4.2 for the zones 1 through 3. The bioreactor sidewater depth is 5.7 m.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The plant treats 9,000 m3/day of flow using primary and biological treatment consisting of two parallel activated sludge trains. The wastewater first enters a primary clarifier and then flow to a biological reactor. Mixed liquor from both trains are combined and discharged into a single secondary clarifier. Ozonation was added to this process by taking sludge from the Return Activated Sludge (RAS), ozonating the sludge, then returning to both reactor trains. The ozonation of the sludge is carried out using the Lyso™ process – a plug flow contactor that enhances the effectiveness of Ozone utilization for lysing bacterial cells.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Ozone added to sludge - 3 kg O3/hr. Supplemental nutrients were added to system for cell growth. During the latter part of period IV, 147 kg N/d was added (as urea or ammonia solution). Phosphorus as phosphoric acid was also added but dose was not specified. Nutrient dosage at the facility is estimated based on the theoretical mass based stoichiometric specification of 200 (COD):5 (N): 1 (P).
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Influent concentrations to secondary treatment: 1,000 mg/l COD, 120 mg/l TSS. Flow rate: 9,000 m3/d.
MANUFACTURER: WEDECO Ozone generator; Praxair Lyso System

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The NAR system consists of a heat exchanger, a CO2 stripper tank, an ammonia stripper, and a scrubber. Pre-treatment such as a cloth screen, screw press, or centrifuge is required. The liquid fraction from the CO2 stripper is treated in the ammonia stripper column where a packing material is used to increase contact surface between liquid and gas phase. The off-gas from the CO2 stripper tank and the ammonia stripper is transported to a scrubbing column. The ammonia stripper uses recirculated air from the scrubber as a carrier gas.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium hydroxide is added to the stripper, sulphuric acid to the scrubber column
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Temperature: 60-75 degrees C
OANDM_COST: Power: 0.36 Euros/kg N removed, Maintenance: 0.18 Euros/kg N removed

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The ADVENT Integral System (AIS) biological treatment system utilizes conventional activated sludge treatment with an integral clarifier. This case study was specifically designed with an additional zone inside the clarifier ring in order to facilitiate denitrification. This zone is mixed with an overhead mixer or can be aerated to provide additional aerobic treatment.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The paper presents a model for estimating biological heat generation and includes monthly operating data for three years, including flow (m3/hr), temperature (degrees C and F), COD (mg/L and kg/day), nitrogen nitrified (kg/d), sludge VSS (%), sludge wasteage (m3/d and kg/d), observed yield (kg/kg), biochemical heat factor (cal/g), HRT (days), and F/M (kg/kg-day)

FGD scrubber blowdown goes through lime chemical pre-treatment. The flow is then clarified with a polymer added for flocculation/coagulation. Next the flow is equalized and sent to ion exchange unit for boron removal. Finally the stream goes through anoxic/anaerobic biological treatment to remove nitrate and selenium and then a final clarifier. Lime is added to the chemical precipitation tanks. There are filters before the IX and before and after the SBR. The anaerobic bio is anaerobic/anoxic for removal of nitrate and selenium and the aerobic SBR (ASG) is to remove residual COD and ammonia before discharge.

ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Hydraulic residence time for the anaerobic reactor is 24 hr.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Process wastewater is initially sent through an oil and water separator. The flow is then equalized and chemicals are added to promote flocculation/coagulation. TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Acrylonitrile and domestic wastewater streams are sent to separate flow equalization basins. The streams are then combined and sent to a mixing basin for grit removal. After a caustic agent is added, the combined stream is sent through the biological double-efficiency process (BDP), consisting of a biofilm airlift suspension reactor, an anaerobic suspended growth chamber, and a clarifier. The BDP unit removes nitrogen from wastewater using an oxygen concentration gradient: ammonia oxidation in the presence of dissolved oxygen and nitrite reduction in very low or zero oxygen levels. Because both nitrification and de-nitrification reactions are occuring in the same unit process, dissolved oxygen levels are kept around 0.3 mg/L. The flocs that are formed prior to entering the unit provide an anoxic environment for microorganisms to reduce nitrite.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Caustic added to mixing basin
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow rate: 1.0 m3/h; hydraulic retention time: 72.25 hr
OANDM_COST: 4.6 Yuan/m3

After the Fenton reagent is added, the stream is sent through dissolved air flotation unit process to remove suspended matter. Stream is again put through advanced oxidation process. Finally, stream is sent to a membrane bioreactor to remove nitrogen.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The influent stream is processed through a disk filtration unit. Disk filtration unit had 10 µm micro-screen panels in a drum configuration. Filter is open to atmosphere and operates under gravity flow conditions. Water is filtered through the peripheral filter panels of the slowly rotating drum. Separated solids are rinsed off the filter screen into the solids collection tray and discharged. The clean water exited the disk filtration tank into an unmixed filtrate tank. The filtrate tank contents were pumped to sewer.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Polymer (starting on Day 22)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Target average flow rate: 2.8 L/s

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The influent stream is sent to a granular media filter unit to treat mercury and suspended solids. Two parallel granular filter systems were mounted on a common platform. After passing through the influent flow assembly, the wastewater flowed into a standpipe at the top of the filter column to provide static liquid head. From the standpipe, the wastewater flowed through the filter media and exited through the bottom of the media to an effluent standpipe. Some water is then used for backwashing, and all effluent is eventually sent to sewer.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Media included anthracite, sand, and garnet. All media had uniformity coefficients of 1.65 or less. Maximum flow rate: 0.17 L/s.

Some water is then used for backwashing, and all effluent is eventually sent to sewer.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Media included anthracite and sand. All media had uniformity coefficients of 1.65 or less. Maximum flow rate: 0.17 L/s.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The influent stream is sent to a granular media filter unit to treat mercury and suspended solids. Two parallel granular filter systems were mounted on a common platform. After passing through the influent flow assembly, the wastewater flowed into a standpipe at the top of the filter column to provide static liquid head. From the standpipe, the wastewater flowed through the filter media and exited through the bottom of the media to an effluent standpipe. Some water is then used for backwashing, and all effluent is eventually sent to sewer.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Media consisted of sand with a uniformity coefficient of 1.65 or less. Maximum flow rate: 0.17 L/s.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater from the Oily Water Sewer is first treated in an API separator to remove large quantities of oil. Next, the stream is sent to an Induced Air Flotation unit, similarly removing dissolved oil & grease but with larger air bubble sizes than a typical DAF unit. Then, the effluent from the IAF is sent to an equalization tank. Finally, the stream is sent to a membrane bioreactor to reduce suspended solids and nitrogen. MBR system has two trains with six cells each. Each cell has a volume of 250 m3.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Phosphoric acid, ferric chloride, acetic acid, spent caustic
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Average flow rate: 784.6 ± 106.8 m3/hr; solids retention time: 30-40 days

INDUSTRY: Canned and preserved fruits and vegetables processing
TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Fruit processing wastewater was delivered in a tote bin to the vinegar plant and a peristaltic pump transferred the wastewater to a 95 L feed tank. Nutrients were added and alkalinity and pH was adjusted by chemical addition in the tote bin or feed tank. A basket strainer with 3 mm perforations screened the wastewater downstream of the feed pump. Influent wastewater was mixed with recycled supernatant/solids from the anaerobic reactor to provide better contact with the solids and buffering of pH, alkalinity, organic loading, and temperature. A 984 L stainless steel tank served as the anaerobic reactor and anaerobic effluent flowed by gravity to an effluent sample container, then was pumped to the aerobic MBR. In the MBR, a type 203 Kubota flat sheet membrane provided liquid/solids separation. Occasional wasting maintained the system at the desired concentration and an aeration scour system provided oxygen for aerobic growth, mixed the biomass, and scoured the membrane cartridges to maintain flux. The permeate was pumped to an effluent sample container. Supernatant was occasionally recycled from the anaerobic reactor to provide better contact with the influent wastewater.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Nutrients are added and alkalinity and pH are adjusted by chemical addition.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The system could treat 57 to 76 liters per day. The anaerobic bioreactor had a 20 day retention time.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The wastewater first goes through preliminary treatment. It then goes through an equalization basin, and 8 units of primary sedimentation. The wastewater then goes through 2 1800 and 3600 m3 anaerobic selectors and 4 oxidation ditch-type activated sludge basins and 9 final clarifiers. The oxidation ditches are fully aerated by a turbo blower/diffuser system.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The system receives 60,000 m3/day of industrial wastewater. The solids retention time was 15 days.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater flow is split between two sets of two extended aeration membrane bioreactor basins arranged in parallel.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 120 hour retention time

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Stripped sour water and oily process water flow into the WWTP.  Operations include primary and secondary oil/water separation, biological treatment in a two-stage activated sludge process with powdered activated carbon addition, tertiary iron coprecipitation, and final pH adjustment. A slipstream of final effluent is sent through the sand filter/GAC system as needed to comply with discharge limits for whole effluent toxicity.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: PAC, PO4, Caustic, FeCL3

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater was pumped to an equalization tank in which pH was adjusted. The WW flows (at rates of 1.5 to 2.5 m^3/hour) to two consecutive Deoxidizing stages for DO uptake, and then followed by an anoxic reactor. Reactors were filled with floating Aqwise Biomass Carriers on which biomass, in the form of biofilm, is present for the biological treatment.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Carbon and phosphorus were dosed to the first deoxidizing reactor.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The carriers fill ratio, in the reactors, was between 20 to 50%. HRT 1.1 - 1.8 hours.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: A multiple stage MBBR process begins with a tailings pond and Actiflo® pre-treatment with metal removal. The process consisted of 4 MBBR in series. The first was aerated to promote the oxidation of cyanide compounds to ammonia. The second reactor was aerated for complete nitrification. The third MBBR used for denitrification, required anoxic conditions and supplemental carbon. The reactor was mechanically mixed using a pendulum mixer and commercially available glucose or glycerin was added as the carbon source. The last MBBR reoxygenated the water.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Hydroxide dosage to maintain pH; C/N ratio between 3 and 6 for carbon dosage; phosphorus dosage for biological growth
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Tank volumes ranged from 100-2100 L.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The treatment train consists of an aerobic MBBR, an anoxic MBBR, and a re-aeration tank. A gravity flow through system was designed to transfer liquid streatm between the reactors. Dissolved oxygen and media mixing of the aerobic reactor were attained by injecting air, whereas, mechanical mixers were used for mixing in the anoxic reactors. Influent was spiked with micro nutrients (metals) and macro nutrients (alkalinity, phosphate).  This treatment train was operated at ambient temperature.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Approximately 1% methanol solution was an external carbon source for denitrification in the anoxic reactors.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Temperature: Ambient; Flow: 5 L/hr; Aerobic Reactor Vol: 20 L; Anoxic Reactor Vol: 13.25 L; Re-aeration Reactor Vol: 2.5 L

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The treatment train consists of an aerobic MBBR, an anoxic MBBR, and a re-aeration tank. A gravity flow through system was designed to transfer liquid streatm between the reactors. Dissolved oxygen and media mixing of the aerobic reactor were attained by injecting air, whereas, mechanical mixers were used for mixing in the anoxic reactors. Influent was spiked with micro nutrients (metals) and macro nutrients (alkalinity, phosphate). This treatment train was operated at 10 degrees C.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Approximately 1% methanol solution was an external carbon source for denitrification in the anoxic reactors.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Temperature: 10 degrees C; Flow: 5 L/hr; Aerobic Reactor Vol: 20 L; Anoxic Reactor Vol: 13.25 L; Re-aeration Reactor Vol: 2.5 L

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater is pumped to the EQ tank which serves to blend, attenuate, and buffer the raw wastewater temperature, pH, COD concentration, and the various cleaning chemicals contained in the wastewater. The water is pumped to two ADI-BVF® reactors in parallel. Effluent from the reactors flow to the aeration tank of the activated sludge system. Aeration provides BOD reduction, nitrification, and sulfide oxidation. The mixed liquor is discharged to the conical-bottom clarifier. Effluent is discharged from the clarifier to the West Boise Sewer District sanitary sewer.  Settled solids from the clarifier are typically returned to the aeration tank as return activated sludge.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: EQ Tank cleaning chemicals: acids, caustic, hydrogen peroxide, peracetic acid
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Average flow: 217,000 gpd; temperature: 24-38 degrees C

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The BAT technology for the Steam Electric ELGs is a chemical precipitation system followed by biological treatment. The chemical precipitation system modeled for the Steam Electric ELGs consisted of an equalization tank, several reaction tanks (for chemical addition), a clarifier, gravity sand filter, an effluent storage tank, a sludge filter press, and a sludge holding tank. The biological treatment system was modeled after the GE ABMet system and consists of an anoxic/anaerobic two stage fixed-film biological system with an activated carbon bed, heat exchanger (for plants in certain locations), oxidation-reduction potential (ORP) monitor, chemical addition system (for ORP control), and denitrification system. The figures represent typical chemical precipitation and biological treatment, but do not necessarily reflect the BAT wastewater treatment train.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: EPA determined that the BAT chemical precipitation system employs hydroxide precipitation, sulfide precipitation, and iron coprecipitation. A molasses-based feed source for the microorganisms is added to the wastewater before entering the biological treatment system. In addition, the biological system contains a chemical addition system that adds reducing agent to control the oxidation reduction potential (ORP).
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Residence times for each piece of equipment were estimated using vendor and plant-specific data. Flow rates are plant-specific and performance data represents the Steam Electric generating industry average for the 69 plants estimated to generate wet FGD wastewater (for coal-fired steam electric units greater than 50 MW).
CAPITAL_COST: $21,884,058 average per plant (2010 dollar basis). Tota Industry Cost is $1.51 billion for 69 plants (TDD, Table 9-6).
OANDM_COST: $1,492,754 average per plant (2010 dollar basis). Total Industry Cost is $103 million for 69 plants (TDD, Table 9-6).

The figures represent typical chemical precipitation and evaporation, but do not necessarily reflect the PSNS wastewater treatment train.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Process wastewater passes through a rotary screen for removal of large solids and grass. Wastewater then moves through a dissolved air flotation (DAF) unit, an aerobic contact and aeration unit, and a second DAF unit with suction sludge withdrawal.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Alum or polyaluminum chloride, sodium hydroxide and/or potassium permanganate may be added to DAF units if needed.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 310 m3/d average plant flow (425 m3/d design flow)
CAPITAL_COST: $2,848,000 total including civil works, equipment cost, and installation
OANDM_COST: $53,898 per year, including chemicals, labor, power, and land costs

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The screens remove solids larger than 1000 um (feathers and bowels) and 750 um (fine solids) from process wastewater. The static screen effluent is collected in a 142 m3-equalization tank before entering a dissolved-air flotation (DAF) system and two upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB) reactors for treatment.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Alkalinity supplementation added to reactors to maintain pH buffering conditions.
OANDM_COST: $0.50 total costs per cubic meter of wastewater treated ($0.17 chemical, $0.10 power, $0.20 staff, $0.03 analytical monitoring)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The AnMBR pilot plant consists of a 200 L stainless steel reactor (500 mm diameter × 1060 mm height) containing a vertical mounted submerged hollow fiber membrane (Zenon ZW-10, approx. 600 mm height and 100 mm diameter, 0.93 m2 surface area). During operation, wastewater flux through the membrane was controlled at a specific rate using a peristaltic pump on the permeate stream. Biogas in the AnMBR was continuously circulated across the membrane surface at a fixed flow rate of 35 L/min (2.3 m3/m2/h1) for fouling control.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The pilot plant was inoculated with digested sludge from an on-site crusted anaerobic lagoon, the methanogenic activity of the inoculum was 0.15 g COD/g VS/d at the time of inoculation. The plant was initially operated at a long hydraulic retention time of 7 days to allow for acclimatization of the anaerobic inoculum. During this initial operation, feed events occurred 2x per week (75 L over 12 h per feed), using a burst feed at relatively high membrane flux to test if the membrane could operate sustainably at flux rates of 6.25 L/m2/h.  Once the biomass was acclimatized and the performance was stable, the plant switched to a continuous operating mode (flux rate of 3.5 L/m2/h during second and third periods of pilot-plant operation). Hydraulic retention time was 4 days during period 2 (40L fed daily over 12 h per feed) and reduced to 2 days during period 3 (80 L/day continuous feed rate).
CAPITAL_COST: Membrane costs estimated at 72% of capital investment
