CAPITAL_COST: Membrane costs estimate at 72% of capital investment

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The treatment system consists of an equalization tank (2.1 m3), a continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR) for facultative predigestion (0.95 m3), a packed bed anaerobic digestion column, and a CSTR activated sludge process (ASP) for effluent polishing (0.95 m3). The packed bed column is cylindrical (1.07 m in diameter and 2.60 m in height) with a total volume of 2.3 m3, with 2.0 m3 packed with a commercial ceramic bio-packing media. The packing material is 1-in Raschig (cylindrical) rings that have 203 m2 m-3 of specific surface area. A recirculation heating pump was utilized to control the influent temperature at 3662 C. Two fine bubble membrane diffusers were used at the bottom of the aeration tank of the ASP. The final clarifier has a volume of 0.605 m3. The waste streams were obtained twice a week from the mill in 0.76 m3 totes. The streams were mixed in the equalization tank before being fed to the facultative predigestion tank where a commercial culture powder was introduced for bio-augmentation (1:5000 bioculture to COD mass ratio) at 12-h HRT. The substrates were then fed continuously into the digester from the predigestion tank.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Culture powder for bio-augmentation, 1:5000 bioculture:COD mass.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The pH in digester was controlled at a neutral range (6.92–7.60) and the digestion occurred at mesophilic temperature (31.5–34.5 C measured in the effluent).
MANUFACTURER: Wisconsin Stamping & Manufacturing, WI, USA (packing material); Stamford Scientific, NY,USA (fine bubble diffusers)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Phase 1: Dairy wastewater from NOOSA yogurt plant and Morning Fresh Dairy is combined, pre-screened using a slope screen, and sent to an equalization tank followed by an aeration basin for BOD removal and nitrification. Alum is added to the aeration basin to aid in chemical precipitation of phosphorus. From the aeration basin, mixed liquor is sent to the MBR system where two membrane tanks operate in parallel. Liquid permeate is extracted through the membrane cartridges prior to recycle or discharge.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Alum is added into the aeration basin to chemically precipitate phosphorus.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design wastewater flow rate: 300 m3/day

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Phase 2: Process wastewater from NOOSA yogurt plant and Morning Fresh Dairy is pre-screened and sent to two hydraulically connected equalization tanks and transferred to the anaerobic basin. Wastewater is temperature adjusted in the forward feed pump to promote phosphorus uptake and reduce alum requirements. Mixed liquor gravity flows from the anaerobic basin to the pre-anoxic basin, in which mixed, unaerated conditions promote denitrification, and is pumped into two aeration basins. Following aeration, wastewater flows to the post-anoxic basin, where carbon sources can be added if necessary to achieve further denitrification, prior to entering an MBR system. MBR effluent is discharged to the effluent cistern for re-aeration prior to discharge or reuse.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Alum is added into aeration basin to chemically precipitate the phosphorus. If necessary, a carbon source can be supplied to the post-anoxic basin to achieve further denitrification to meet the effluent TN limit of 14.84 mg/L.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design wastewater flow rate: 600 m3/day

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: System included combined chemical precipitation and MF skid, as well as two different polishing treatment trains. The first polishing train, operated for the entire six-week pilot test, included four ion exchange vessels in series (two zeolite resin vessels and two strong acid cation resin vessels). The second polishing treatment train was operated for the second half of the pilot test, and included two stages of reverse osmosis. Other intermediate processes included pH adjustment and pumping. The MF skid, was an eight-tube pilot microfiltration unit, combined with chemical precipitation capability. Performance data does not include reverse osmosis treatment.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Ferric chloride, 35% as FeCl3 (diluted to 7% to 10.5%, or 100 grams/liter to 150 grams/liter for use) was added at the first reaction tank of MF skid; Sodium sulfide, 15% as Na2S (diluted to 10 grams/liter to 15 grams/liter for use), was added to the second reaction tank beginning the second week of the test;  Sodium hydroxide, 50% as NaOH, was added at second reaction tank of MF skid;  Sulfuric acid, 93% as H2SO4 (diluted to 4% to 20% for use), was added in the third chemical reaction tank (pH adjustment tank); Powdered activated carbon slurry, 10 grams/liter was added to the first reaction tank for one week of the test.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Influent flow rates (0.13-0.19 L/s) over six week testing period, MF skid will include three small reaction chambers, each with 190 L capacity for chemical addition and precipitation, and a concentrate tank with 380 L capacity. Eight tubular microfilter membrane modules, each 2.54 cm (1 inch) in diameter with total membrane area per module of 0.14 m2 (1.5 square feet).

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: FGD blowdown is first sent to physical/chemical treatment using a combination of coagulants and pH adjustments within a clarifier to reduce amount of filter cake. Next, micro-filtration prepares water for RO separation. RO advanced membrane separation ensures high water recoveries and efficient water re-use. The final step, membrane polishing, uses brackish water RO to increase final permeate purity. Performance data represents results from the optimum runs in Weeks 4 and 5.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Low pH sulfate precipitant plus aluminum based Coagulant - clarification - 173 gal/week (week 1), Low pH sulfate precipitant plus Coagulant - 74 gal/week (week 2), High pH sulfate precipitant with coagulant - 133 gal/week (week 3), Coagulant with anti-scale only - 58 gal/week (week 4), Coagulant with anti-scale only - 37 gal/week (week 5). During this trial, an aluminum based coagulant was used as the primary coagulant along with a proprietary formulation for scale inhibition prior to the RO.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: During optimal conditions, 7,001 gallons were treated resulting in ~87% average water recovery.
OANDM_COST: Physical / Chemical treatment: < $0.011 per gallon average, Membrane Replacement (Estimated Quarterly replacement): < $0.004 per gallon

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Physical/chemical treatment using combination of coagulants and pH adjustments within a clarifier to reduce amount of filter cake. Micro-filtration (membrane filtration in codes) prepares water for RO separation (these two steps make up pretreatment). RO advanced membrane separation ensures high water recoveries and efficient water re-use. The final step membrane polishing using brackish water RO enables certain ELG/local permit guarantees.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: For the duration of the pilot test, the system yielded an average permeate recovery of 92%.
OANDM_COST: Physical/chemical treatment: < $0.011 per gallon, Membrane replacement: <$0.004 per gallon (estimated quarterly replacement)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The ZLD system is an addition to the primary refinery process wastewater treatment system (a traditional system composed of O/W separation followed by bio treatment).  The effluent from this system is combined with cooling water tower blowdown and various backwash streams and fed to the ZLD system, composed of equalization, clarification, multimedia filtration, ultrafiltration, reverse osmosis, and brine concentration.  The resultant effluent stream is recycled to the cooling tower. It appears some slipstreams from the system may be discharged.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Non-Oxidizing biocide is injected into the water before it enters the RO Feed Tank to control the residual organics and the excess chlorine is removed from this water using Sodium Bisulfate before entering the RO membranes, as chlorine damages the RO membranes. To prevent scaling, scale inhibitor chemical injection is provided in RO feed water.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: One pass - Three stage RO membrane system has flux rate of 37.7 l/m2/hr.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The process involved heating the water to simulate field temperature of the produced water, then treating the water with electrocoagulation. Clarification was performed utilizing a Dissolved Air Floatation (DAF) process. The final process steps utilizing Ultra Filtration (UF) and Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) were applied for fine filtration and polishing.
CAPITAL_COST: Skidded EC, DAF, UF and GAC - $5,800,000, Storage & Process Tanks - $3,200,000, Facility - $2,800,000, Total - $11,800,000
OANDM_COST: Treatment Consumables - $3,193,750 annually, Labor - $638,750 annually, Power - $91,250 annually, Total - $3,923,750 annually

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Reject recovery from reverse osmosis (RO) treatment was utilized for the evaluation. The pH was amended, treated with EC, aerated, filtered by ultrafiltration (UF), and pH was amended again to meet a discharge specification of 7 pH. The RO was run at 50 percent recovery using a GE SEPA cell with an AD (desalination) membrane.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Initial pH adjustment was done to raise pH using 50% sodium hydroxide. EC cells were provided for iron dosage and hydrochloric acid was used to lower the pH in the system.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Mining facility requested treatment of 100 gpm of reject recovery RO water to reduce the Silica concentration, reported as SiO, from 220 mg/l to less than 60 mg/l as feed water for a Reject Recovery Reverse-Osmosis (RRRO).
CAPITAL_COST: Containerized Equipment (EC and UF) - $320,000, Skidded High Pressure RO & CIP - $97,500, Total cost - $417,000
OANDM_COST: Sodium Hydroxide (50%) - $70,702 annual, EC Cells - $210,700 annual, Hydrochloric Acid (37%) - $12,463, Power - $60,181, Total operational cost - $354,047

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater generated from metal finishing processes undergoes mechanical pre-treatment using strainers. Then, wastewater is transferred to an equalization tank where sodium bisulfite is added to the wastewater in order to reduce Cr (VI) to Cr (III) and H2SO4 is also added to reduce the pH to 3 and accelerate the reaction. The reacted wastewater is then transferred to the reaction tank where caustic soda is added, and pH is increased up to 8.2-8.5. Chromium and other metals precipitate. This tank is a continuously stirred-tank reactor (CSTR) of 45 min hydraulic residence time (HRT). The reacted wastewater is then transferred to a concentrate tank where solids are removed. A feed pump then transfers the reacted wastewater to the membrane recirculation loop. The recirculation loop consists of a recirculation pump and two membranes in series.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium bisulfite, H2SO4, caustic soda
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The reaction tank is a continuously stirred-tank reactor (CSTR) of 45 min hydraulic residence time (HRT). Three different types of membranes were tested during the pilot study with a cut-off ranging from 50 nm to 0.1 micrometers.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Influent feed water from six mines is collected in a feed water tank.  The treatment process consists of two oxidation tanks in series,  lime and soda ash softening, clarification, pH adjustment (addition of acid and sodium hypochlorite), multimedia filtration (seven vertical pressure filters operated in parallel), reverse osmosis (5-micron cartridge filtration followed by five parallel skids), and final effluent remineralization (using carbon dioxide and lime water).
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Ferric chloride (inline prior to first oxidation tank), lime (softening tank), soda ash (softening tank), acid (pH adjustment tank), sodium hypochlorite (pH adjustment tank), antiscalant (inline prior to RO), sodium bisulfite (inline prior to RO)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Two oxidation tanks operating in series provide a total residence time of approximately 27 minutes at maximum design flow conditions. The softening tank is designed to provide a residence time of approximately 30 minutes at maximum design flow conditions. The pH adjustment tank is designed to provide a residence time of approximately 15 minutes at maximum design flow. The multimedia filters each have a three foot filter bed comprised of layers of garnet, sand, and anthracite with a gravel underdrain.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: First, wastewater flows through two oxidation tanks in series. Ferric chloride is sometimes added inline prior to the first oxidation tank. Air is added to both oxidation tanks. Effluent from the second oxidation tank overflows into the adjacent softening tank, where lime and soda ash softening is performed. The effluent from the softening tank flows by gravity to Clarifier 1.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Ferric chloride, lime, soda ash
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The two oxidation tanks operating in series provide a total residence time of approximately 27 minutes at maximum design flow conditions.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater first enters a full-scale membrane bioreactor (MBR) that uses a biological system (configured for nitrification and denitrification) and an ultrafiltration membrane. Then, wastewater undergoes ion exchange softening for barium removal. The barium, along with calcium and magnesium, will exchange with the sodium ions of the resin. Finally, the wastewater goes through reverse osmosis (RO).
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Influent flow rate is on average 120 gpm and maximum 120 gpm. The hydraulic retention time for the MBR biological system design was 41.6 hours. The RO system was designed to treat 117 gpm.
MANUFACTURER: SUEZ Water Technologies & Solutions Membrane Bioreactor (MBR) utilizing ZeeWeed* 500D

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: There are a series of three hybrid Zero Valent Iron (hZVI) reactors, where ferrous chloride (FeCl2) is added to each reactor. Wastewater then moves to an aeration tank where compressed air and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is added. Next, the wastewater moves to another tank where a polymer is added for flocculation. Finally, the wastewater is moved to a clarifier, where sludge is removed.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Ferrous chloride (FeCl2), Sodium hydroxide (NaOH), Polymer
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The average feed to the hZVI system was 41 gpm.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Refinery wastewater is pumped to primary oil-water separators followed by a secondary dissolved gas flotation (DGF) system. DGF system effluent was sent to an activated sludge system. Performance data was measured at influent and effluent of primary oil-water separators only.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Polyaluminum chloride (PAC) to the primary OWS system

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Pilot system included one feed tank equipped with a mechanical mixer to receive dissolved gas flotation (DGF) effluent. The feed tank volume was 1,000 L.  DGF effluent entered the feed tank by gravity from a skimmer tank, followed by treatment through a two stage MBBR. Performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the MBBR units only.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Study included consistent addition of spent caustic during the Average and Peak Conditions phases. Study also mentioned addition of 20% NH4CI and supplemental COD spike. The spent caustic was metered to the feed tank at the rate of 1.7-2.3 L/hour. Water drawn from crude oil storage tank was added occasionally to provide supplemental COD to achieve 275 mg/L COD goal at pilot units. Supplemental TKN and was added to the pilot influent in the form of NH4Cl solution (54,000 mg/L NH3-N). The NH4Cl solution was pumped from a 1,000 L tote at a rate of 0.5-0.62 L/hr.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Two-stage MBBR: Flow rate = 0.8 m3/hr., Temperature = 25.0 C, HRT = 5.8 hr.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Pilot system included one feed tank equipped with a mechanical mixer to receive dissolved gas flotation (DGF) effluent. The feed tank volume was 1,000 L.  DGF effluent entered the feed tank by gravity from a skimmer tank, followed by treatment through a two stage FBBR. Performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the FBBR units only.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Study included consistent addition of spent caustic during the Average and Peak Conditions phases. Study also mentioned addition of 20% NH4CI and supplemental COD spike. The spent caustic was metered to the feed tank at the rate of 1.7-2.3 L/hour. Water drawn from crude oil storage tank was added occasionally to provide supplemental COD to achieve 275 mg/L COD goal at pilot units. Supplemental TKN and was added to the pilot influent in the form of NH4Cl solution (54,000 mg/L NH3-N). The NH4Cl solution was pumped from a 1,000 L tote at a rate of 0.5-0.62 L/hr.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Two-stage FBBR: Flow rate = 0.2 m3/hr., Temperature = 24.2 C, HRT = 9.0 hr.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 15: Treatment consists of sodium hypochlorite (0.8%) and permanganate addition followed by greensand filters. Then, lime and klenphos (a corrosion inhibitor) are added, respectively.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium hypochlorite 0.8% and permanganate are dosed prior to sand filters. Lime and klenphos are dosed after the sand filters.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 16: Treatment consists of chlorine dioxide followed by hypochlorous/hypochlorite addition.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Chlorine dioxide; Hypochlorous/hypochlorite

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 17: Treatment consists of intake screens, coagulation/flocculation/clarification, ozonation, sand filtration (with some pre-chlorination), then chlorination followed by pH adjustment.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Potassium permanganate is sometimes dosed to the influent, but was not in use during the sampling dates; post-chlorine dosing to the effluent is about 2.27-2.33 parts per million (ppm)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow rate is between 50 to 55 MGD.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 18: Treatment consists of an aeration packed tower, followed by granulated activated carbon (GAC) filtration and hypochlorite addition.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Hypochlorite is dosed to the GAC effluent
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The #1 basin holds 750,000 gallons and the #2 holds 500,000 gallons. At a rate of 5.0 mgd, the detention time is around 5.8 hours. The 8 GAC towers hold 20,000 lbs of Calgon F300 each. The GAC is replaced with virgin GAC approximately every 5 years, but samples for this study were taken with carbon that has been utilized for about 6 years.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 19: Treatment consists of hypochlorous/hypochlorite addition.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Hypochlorous/hypochlorite

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 5: Treatment consists of a magnetic anion exchange high rate system, followed by coagulation, flocculation, and sedimentation; microfiltration, and hypochlorous/hyplochlorite addition.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Hypochlorous/hyplochlorite is dosed to the final effluent
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The flow rate is 3 MGD. The hydraulic residence time is 6 minutes.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 7: Water is pumped to the main treatment facility where it undergoes caustic softening followed by solids contact clarification. Next, it undergoes UV/AOP treatment including hydrogen peroxide addition. Following UV/AOP, the water is sent through two biologically-active GAC filters. The water is then treated by six GAC contact adsorbers.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Caustic is dosed at the start of treatment for softening; hydrogen peroxide is dosed for UV/AOP treatment: 4 mg/L
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Average flow rate is about 5 MGD. The GAC filters are equipped with 780 ft3 of Norit 816 activated carbon. The GAC contact adsorbers have a designed empty bed contact time of about 10 minutes and each contains 858 ft3 of Norit GAC300. The UV system has a design dose >500 MJ/cm2.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 8: Treatment begins with primary sedimentation (alum and polymer are added for coagulation) and flocculation. From the sedimentation basins, the water travels to 47 sand filters. Sand filter effluent is sent to the GAC system, consisting of 12 contactors. Final effluent is dosed with hypochlorous/hypochlorite.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Alum and polymer are dosed to the influent for coagulation. GAC effluent is dosed with hypochlorous/hypochlorite.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Sand filters have flow rate of 6 MGD and filtration rate of 3 gallons per minute per square foot (gpm/ft2). The GAC system has an empty bed contact time of at least 15 minutes with flow varying from 10 MGD to 18 MGD.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Influent raw craft brewery wastewater was first diluted, then entered into the SSAnMBR system (suspended solids AnMBR), which used a mechanically mixed digester with mixed liquor recirculated between the digester and an external coupled membrane tank.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium bicarbonate to control pH
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Temperatures were controlled at 37 degrees C, membrane operation flux was set at 8 L/m2/hr. Permeation controlled feeding resulting in HRT of 44 hours. SRT controlled at 50 days by sludge wasting.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The treatment process begins with solid-liquid separation using a drum screen followed by a primary clarifier. The primary effluent is equalized before being treated in an EcoVolt (a bioelectrically-enhanced anaerobic digestion process) to reduce BOD5. A majority of the EcoVolt effluent is pumped to a membrane bioreactor (MBR), which utilizes two nano bubble generators (NBGs), where the remainder of the BOD5 is removed. The MBR permeate is discharged to the collection system along with any EcoVolt effluent that bypasses the MBR. Performance data only apply to the aeration system and MBR.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Nitrogen is added to the MBR to maintain the carbon to nitrogen to phosphorus (C:N:P) ratio required by the activated sludge process.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Average influent flowrate is 13,509 gal/day. Peak influent flow is 18,900 gal/day. Average hydraulic residence time is 3.1 days. Peak hydraulic residence time is 2.6 days.
MANUFACTURER: Nanobubble generators are manufactured by Moleaer, Inc.
OANDM_COST: $76,500 (est.)/year for MBR aeration system

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater from the brewery is pre-screened using an externally-fed rotary drum screen, and screened liquid is discharged to an equalization tank. A recirculation loop was used to mix the equalization tank contents and monitor pH while adding supplemental alkalinity. Conditioned wastewater is pumped to the insulated, bolted steel continuously-stirred tank reactor (CSTR). The anaerobic biomass in the CSTR remove the bulk of the organic load in the combined brewery wastewater (process wastewater and spent hops/yeast). The CSTR is mixed with two side-entry mixers to maintain solids in suspension and ensure good biomass-to-substrate contact. Effluent is screened by a single membrane tank housing double-deck flat-plate membrane cassettes used for solids/liquid separation and biomass retention. Permeate extracted from the membrane cassettes is discharged to the Buncombe County municipal treatment plant.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Supplemental alkalinity is dosed into the equalization tank.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design anaerobic membrane bioreactor average flow: 117,250 gal/day. Peak anaerobic membrane bioreactor flow: 142,150 gal/day. Membrane pore size is 0.2 um.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: [Facility A] The influent was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS), biological phosphorus removal, and tertiary filtration with anthracite. The non-disinfected water was then fed to the pilot plant and ozonated. Additional treatment followed the ozonation, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the ozonation.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Ozonation occurred at a dose of mg ozone to mg total organic carbon of 1.5-2.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: [Facility B] The influent was pretreated with conventional activated sludge (CAS), tertiary filtration, and disinfection with chlorine. The disinfected wastewater was then treated with microfiltration. Additional treatment followed the microfiltration, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the microfiltration.

[Facility C] Influent was treated at a full-scale plant by conventional activated sludge (CAS), biological phosphorus removal, and tertiary filtration with anthracite and sand. Tertiary effluent was fed to the pilot scale treatment process including ozonation. Additional treatment followed the ozonation, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the ozonation.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Ozonation occurred at a dose of mg ozone to mg total organic carbon of 0.8.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: [Facility D] Influent to the pilot scale system was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS) and tertiary filtration with sand. Tertiary effluent was fed to the pilot scale treatment system including ozonation. Additional treatment followed ozonation, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the ozonation.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Ozonation occurred at a dose of mg ozone to mg total organic carbon of about 1.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: [Facility A] The influent to the pilot plant was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS), biological phosphorus removal, and tertiary filtration with anthracite. The non-disinfected water was then fed to the pilot plant, ozonated, and filtered by biologically activated carbon (BAC). Additional treatment followed the BAC, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the BAC.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The BAC was operated at an empty bed contact time of 16 minutes.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: [Facility A] The influent to the pilot plant was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS), biological phosphorus removal, and tertiary filtration with anthracite. The non-disinfected water was then fed to the pilot plant, ozonated, filtered by biologically activated carbon (BAC), and treated by two parallel microfiltration and ultrafiltration membranes, which were chloraminated. Additional treatment followed the microfiltration, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to microfiltration, prior to combination with the ultrafiltration effluent.

[Facility A] The influent to the pilot plant was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS), biological phosphorus removal, and tertiary filtration with anthracite. The non-disinfected water was then fed to the pilot plant, ozonated, filtered by biologically activated carbon (BAC), and treated by two parallel microfiltration and ultrafiltration membranes, which were chloraminated. Additional treatment followed  ultrafiltration, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to ultrafiltration, prior to combination with the microfiltration effluent.

[Facility C] Influent was treated at a full-scale plant by conventional activated sludge (CAS), biological phosphorus removal, and tertiary filtration with anthracite and sand. Tertiary effluent was fed to the pilot scale treatment process including ozonation and two parallel biologically active carbon filters (BAC).  Additional treatment followed the BAC, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the BAC.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Biologically active carbon filters were operated at empty bed contact times of 10 minutes and were acclimated on site for 8 months prior to installation.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: [Facility D] Influent to the pilot scale system was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS) and tertiary filtration with sand. Tertiary effluent was fed to the pilot scale treatment system including ozonation and a biologically active carbon (BAC) filter. Additional treatment followed the BAC, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the BAC.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The biologically active filter was run at an empty bed contact time of 15 minutes.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: [Facility D] Influent to the pilot scale system was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS) and tertiary filtration with sand. Tertiary effluent was fed to the pilot scale treatment system including ozonation, a biologically active carbon (BAC) filter, and ultrafiltration. Additional treatment followed the ultrafiltration, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the ultrafiltration.

[Facility D] Influent to the system was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS) and tertiary filtration with sand. The pilot scale treatment system consisted of ozonation, a biologically active filter, ultrafiltration, and granular activated carbon (GAC). Additional treatment followed the GAC, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the GAC.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The granular activated carbon (GAC) unit was operated at an empty bed contact time of 15 minutes.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: [Facility A] The influent to the pilot plant was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS), biological phosphorus removal, and tertiary filtration with anthracite. The non-disinfected water was then fed to the pilot plant, ozonated, filtered by biologically activated carbon (BAC), and treated by two parallel microfiltration and ultrafiltration membranes, which were chloraminated. The membrane effluent was combined and then treated by reverse osmosis (RO). Additional treatment followed RO, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to RO.

[Facility A] The influent to the pilot plant was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS), biological phosphorus removal, and tertiary filtration with anthracite. The non-disinfected water was then fed to the pilot plant, ozonated, filtered by biologically activated carbon (BAC), and treated by two parallel microfiltration and ultrafiltration membranes, which were chloraminated. The membrane effluent was combined and then treated by reverse osmosis (RO) and an ultraviolet advanced oxidation process (UV/AOP). The performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the UV/AOP process.

[Facility B] The influent was pretreated with conventional activated sludge (CAS), tertiary filtration, and disinfection with chlorine. The disinfected wastewater was then treated with microfiltration and reverse osmosis (RO). Additional treatment followed RO, but the performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to RO.

[Facility B] The influent was pretreated with conventional activated sludge (CAS), tertiary filtration, and disinfection with chlorine. The disinfected wastewater was then treated with microfiltration, reverse osmosis (RO), and an ultraviolet advanced oxidation process (UV/AOP). The performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the UV/AOP.

[Facility C] Influent was treated at a full-scale plant by conventional activated sludge (CAS), biological phosphorus removal, and tertiary filtration with anthracite and sand. Tertiary effluent was fed to the pilot scale treatment process including ozonation and two parallel biologically active carbon (BAC) filters . Effluent from the two BAC filters were combined and treated by a granular activated carbon (GAC) adsorber. Performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the GAC.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The GAC operated at empty bed contact time (EBCT) of 10 minutes.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: [Facility D] Influent to the pilot scale system was pretreated at a full-scale plant with conventional activated sludge (CAS) and tertiary filtration with sand. Tertiary effluent was fed to the pilot scale treatment system including ozonation, a biologically active carbon (BAC) filter, ultrafiltration, granular activated carbon (GAC), and an ultraviolet advanced oxidation process (UV/AOP). Performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the AOP.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Hydrogen peroxide was dosed to the UV/AOP at 10 mg/L.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 10: Sodium hypochlorite and ammonium hydroxide are initially added to create an average of 3 mg/L chloramines. The flow then splits between an ultrafiltration (UF) membrane and a microfiltration (MF) membrane operated in parallel. The MF/UF product water is combined in a common break tank and then fed to two parallel reverse osmosis (RO) trains. Antiscalant is added before the RO membranes. RO permeate water is combined and hydrogen peroxide is added. A UV reactor is used on the final permeate.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium hypochlorite and ammonium hydroxide are dosed to the influent; antiscalant is dosed prior to RO filtration; hydrogen peroxide is dosed to the RO permeate at 3 ppm
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The MF and UF are both operated at 29-30 gfd and 93-95% recovery. RO flux rate is 11.6 to 11.9 gfd and recovery is 80%. UV flow rate is 700 gpm.
MANUFACTURER: UF: Toray; MF: Pall Water; RO: Toray and Hydranautics; UV system: Trojan UVPhox

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 11: Water from several sources is aerated before being blended together. Two rapid mix stations follow, with hydrated lime and chlorine dioxide added to the first station, and hydrated lime slurry, carbon dioxide, and aluminum sulfate added to the second. The water then undergoes flocculation, followed by sedimentation. The next step is anthracite/sand filtration, and hydrated lime slurry, chlorine gas, and anionic polyacrylamide (an anionic polymer) are injected into the water. After filtration, the water travels to the clear well where chlorine gas is added.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: During rapid mix process, 9.20 mg/L hydrated lime and 0.50 mg/L ClO2 are added to the first station, and 25.8 mg/L hydrated lime slurry, 20.0 mg/L CO2, and aluminum sulfate are added to the second station.  During anthracite/sand filtration, 2.6 mg/L hydrated lime slurry, 0.95 mg/L Cl2 gas, and anionic polyacrylamide (an anionic polymer) are injected into the water. After filtration, 1.75 mg/L Cl2 gas is added to the clear well.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 12: The plant utilizes pH adjustment with sulfuric acid (when required), pre-ozonation, coagulation with powdered activated carbon (when needed for taste and odor control), high rate dissolved air flotation (DAF) for pre-filter solids removal, chlorination, dual media filters, pH adjustment with caustic (corrosion control), and secondary disinfection with chloramines. The ozone system includes ozone generation using liquid oxygen and ozone dissolution using submerged diffusers.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sulfuric acid is dosed to the influent; caustic is dosed to the dual media filter effluent
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Average flow is about 110 mgd from a reservoir supply that has a 200 mgd capacity. Submerged diffusers have a contact time of about 10 minutes.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 13: Treatment consists of UV followed by hypochlorous/hypochlorite addition.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Hypochlorous/hypochlorite is dosed to the UV effluent
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: UV system, Aquaray H2O by Ozonia, has 2 reactors each capable of treating 3 mgd with a dosage of 80 mJ/cm2, and the UV transmittance is 95%.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 14: Water is first treated using anion exchange and dosed with an arsenic removal resin. Then, a polyphosphate is added to control scaling and sequester iron. Water then goes through an aeration tower for volatile organic compound (VOC) removal, and then into the clear well where sodium hypochlorite is added.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Polyphosphate is dosed to the ion exchange resin: 2 gallons/day; hypochlorite is dosed to the final effluent: 5-7 gallons/day
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The treatment system flow rate is 350 gpm.
MANUFACTURER: Anion exchange media: Purolite; Polyphosphate (C-18): Coyne

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The treatment system consists of three steps: a forward osmosis (FO) system, a "modified" RO process, and seawater RO system. Diluted draw from FO is sent to the modified RO process. This RO fully recovers the draw and returns it to FO. Permeate from the modified RO process is sent to the seawater RO system, which partially recovers the draw solution and returns it to the modified RO process.
OANDM_COST: Energy use: 9.9 kWh/m3

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: BioGill technology is an above ground, non-submerged bioreactor providing attached growth planar media for microorganisms. The media is configured to provide two distinct regions, air and liquid, by folding the media sheet over a top hanger bar creating an inside air pocket. Wastewater is fed from spiral spray nozzles located at the top and flows downward by gravity through the liquid side. The treatment system includes a balance tank with a mixer and a transfer pump, followed by a recirculation tank that sends wastewater to a solar water heat exchanger. Both the balance tank and recirculation tanks are pH balanced. Effluent from the heat exchanger feeds into 9 BioGill modules. Sludge is removed from the modules and sent to a sludge pit, and effluent wastewater is recirculated and discharged.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Urea, phosphoric acid
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design flow: 20 m3/day (5,300 gpd); balance tank volume: 60 m3 (16,000 gal); recirculation tank volume: 30 m3 (8,000 gal)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The source water for the pilot was a waste neutralization cascade, a treatment system that combines production broths and cleaning solutions. A portion of the waste stream, combined with city water, was pumped through a heat exchanger prior to the microfiltration feed tank. The feed to the system was pumped to a microfiltration skid which was equipped with full-scale PVDF hollow fiber membrane modules. Permeate was then pumped to a reverse osmosis (RO) skid with three full scale reverse osmosis spiral wound membranes.
MEDIA_TYPE: Microfiltration: PVDF hollow fiber membrane modules; Reverse Osmosis: spiral wound membranes
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Microfiltration unit flow rate was 20 gpm and the membranes had a nominal pore size of 1.0 microns. The reverse osmosis unit flow rate was 10 gpm and the three membranes had 8-inch diameters (440 square feet surface area).
MANUFACTURER: Microfiltration unit: Pall Corporation; Reverse osmosis unit: Desalitech; Reverse osmosis membranes: DOW Filmtec

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: A reverse osmosis (RO) unit using low energy membranes treated permeate from a membrane bioreactor.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Reverse osmosis unit was run at 73% to 74% recovery at a flux rate of 8 to 10 gallons per square feet per day (gfd).

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Utility 4: Secondary effluent wastewater is dosed with a chloramine residual prior to microfiltration (MF). The MF process is followed by Reverse Osmosis (RO) and an Advanced Oxidation Process (AOP) using ultraviolet light. Following AOP there is a post treatment process consisting of partial decarbonation and hydrated lime addition for final product water stabilization.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: The treatment system influent is dosed with chloramine. The RO system is pre-dosed with sulfuric acid for pH reduction and anti-scalant for mineral scale control. AOP is dosed with hydrogen peroxide at a dose of 3 mg/L. Hydrated lime is dosed to the AOP effluent.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: MF is operated at 20.4 gallons per square foot per day (gfd) and is backwashed every 22 minutes with a full cleaning every three weeks. Permeate flow from the MF is 86 million gallons per day (MGD). The RO system has a flux of 12 gfd with 85 percent recovery. The RO system has a permeate of 70 MGD and the UV system also has a total capacity of 70 MGD.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Influent to the treatment train was brine from one pass of a reverse osmosis (RO) system that treated raw produced water from an oil field. The brine was sent through the forward osmosis (FO) and membrane distillation treatment train, which was initially operated under once-through (pre-concentration) mode to increase the feed TDS to 105,500 ppm. Only the FO concentrate was recycled to the feed tank during this time. The effluent was stored in a concentrated feed tank. Then, the operation mode was changed to continuous mode with the stored water serving as influent, with the MD permeate also recirculated to the FO feed tank. Performance data is taken from row 1 of Tables 1 and 2, which is assumed to correspond to the first run described in the paper with sodium chloride used as the draw solution.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: 4.5 M NaCl FO draw solution
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Overall production rate varied from 130 to 325 gpd
CAPITAL_COST: Projected full-scale cost: $18.9 MM for 4.5 MGD plant
OANDM_COST: Projected full scale cost: $2.49 MM/year for 4.5 MGD plant

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Approximately 100 m3 of mine wastewater was shipped to the pilot plant location where the Selen-IX system was installed to remove selenium from the feed water. Initially, the feed water transferred into a pre-treatment filtration unit where ferric iron was added to precipitate selenite and TSS from the feed water. The effluent from the pre-treatment filtration compartment was then sent to the ion exchange unit for further removal of selenium. Finally, the spent regenerant from the ion exchange chamber was transferred to the electroreduction circuit (ERC) unit where additional removal of selenium took place. The residue was converted into stable solids. Treated regenerate from ERC unit was recycled back to the ion exchange chamber.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Gypsum and selenate were added to the primary feed water to match water chemistry predicted by geochemical modeling. Following the chemical spiking and before the usage of selen-IX, approximately 10 mg/L of ferric iron was added to feed water to precipitate selenite.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: 100 m3 of feed water was used in three phases of this pilot study.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Selen-IX system was used to remove selenium from the three different feed waters (existing, high selenium feed water, and high sulfate feed water) originated from a Canadian mining site. Initially, the feed water transferred into a pre-treatment filtration unit where ferric iron was added to precipitate selenite and TSS from the feed water. The effluent from the pre-treatment filtration compartment was then sent to the ion exchange unit for further removal of selenium. Finally, the spent regenerant from the ion exchange chamber was transferred to the electroreduction circuit (ERC) unit where additional removal of selenium took place. The residue was converted into stable solids. Treated regenerate from ERC unit was recycled back to the ion exchange chamber.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Ferric iron is added as a part of Selen-IX pretreatment filtration system. During the second phase, the feed water was spiked with selenium to 0.100 mg/L (as selenate). During the third phase, the feed water was spiked with sulfate to 4,000 mg/L.
OANDM_COST: Cost of consumables (power, iron, sodium sulfate): $0.45/m3

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater from existing DAF system at the facility was sent to the pilot influent tank. A mixer was installed in the influent tank to ensure solids did not settle and grease did not float, creating a representative, consistent feed to the pilot system. From the influent tank, the effluent was pumped to first anoxic tank (Tank 1) by a submersible pump, flowed to the first aerobic tank (Tank 2A) and then to an identical second aerobic tank (Tank 2B) by gravity. Both aerobic tanks were aerated continuously by plant air initially and then by dedicated blowers. A portion of effluent from Tank 2A was recycled back to the first anoxic tank (Tank 1) (mixed liquor recycle). Via an underflow pipe, water was discharged from Tank 2B to the second anoxic tank (Tank 3). Overflow water from Tank 3 then passed into an aerated MBR tank by gravity. Mixed liquor was wasted by pumping to the wasting tank. A second mixed liquor return stream (MLR #2) was pumped back to Tank 1 via a submersible pump located in the MBR tank to prevent solids concentrating in the MBR tank.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: pH was controlled initially by the addition of sodium bicarbonate and later in the study by sodium hydroxide (caustic) solution automatically dosed. Phosphorus was added into the first aerobic tank (Tank 2A). Later in the study, a glycerin-based carbon supplement (MicroC1000) was added to Tank 3 at a target flow rate of 5 L/d for 2.0 L/min influent flow.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Design flow rate of 1.7 L/min. Overall capacity for the pilot study (two anoxic and two aerobic tanks) was 8.4 m3.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The full-scale treatment system consisted of six basins in series including an inlet tank and MBR tanks for solids separation. The five basins after the inlet tank were divided into two parallel treatment trains to allow for easier maintenance and flexibility for flow and loading variation. Each train was designed to treat 50 percent of the design basis flow and loadings. Pre-treated DAF effluent flowed to the feed and pumped to the 200 m3 inlet tank. Wastewater flowed by gravity from the influent tank to each treatment train through adjustable overflow weirs. Within each train, the wastewater flowed through adjustable overflow weirs sequentially from the first anoxic stage to the primary aeration stage, to the second anoxic stage, and the re-aeration basin. From the re-aeration tank, the wastewater flowed by gravity to the MBR tanks via a submerged pipe to help prevent scum, foam, and potential grease spills/accumulations from fouling the MBR membranes. Effluent was pumped through the MBR via permeate pumps to the effluent storage lagoon. The first stage (from the primary aerobic tanks) and second stage (from the MBR tanks) mixed liquor recycle (MLR) flows from both trains were combined and mixed with the DAF effluent in the inlet tank.
MEDIA_TYPE: Submerged polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) braided hollow fiber type membranes
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Phosphoric acid was added for macro nutrient supplementation, Micro C for carbon supplementation in the second stage anoxic tanks, and caustic for supplemental alkalinity and pH adjustment.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Volume of each tank: primary anoxic tank - 1500 m3; aeration tank - 6000 m3; secondary anoxic tank - 1500 m3; re-aeration tank - 320 m3; and MBR tank - 136 m3.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The Streamwise technology is an advanced DAF technology that incorporates artificial intelligence to achieve optimized DAF operation and address a variety of effluents. There are two model-driven algorithms that dictate the dosing of chemicals for consistent and effective performance: AI-driven TSS optimization and model-based optimal pH control. Dairy processing wastewater goes into a DAF system.  An on-site embedded PC stores and processes the data from the sensors; the data is then transmitted and further processed into a cloud-based platform. An iOS and Android based app are used for tracking the system performance. A remote monitoring team tracks the system, triaging system alarms to screen out nuisance alarms, identifying root causes, and implementing corrective actions either remotely or through site operator intervention.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Chemicals (caustic soda, acids, coagulant, flocculant) were added by artificial intelligence and model system for TSS and pH control, but amounts were not specified.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow rate is 40 – 100 m3/hr., 12 – 24 hr./day; hourly automatic cleaning of the sensors are specified.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The Streamwise technology is an advanced DAF technology that incorporates artificial intelligence to achieve optimized DAF operation and address a variety of effluents. There are two model-driven algorithms that dictate the dosing of chemicals for consistent and effective performance. Cereal processing wastewater goes into a DAF system.  An on-site embedded PC stores and processes the data from the sensors; the data is then transmitted and further processed into a cloud-based platform. An iOS and Android based app are used for tracking the system performance. CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Chemicals (caustic soda, acids, coagulant, flocculant) were added by artificial intelligence and model system for TSS and pH control, but amounts were not specified.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow rate is 4 – 8 m3/hr., 8 – 20 hr./day.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: The Streamwise technology is an advanced DAF technology that incorporates artificial intelligence to achieve optimized DAF operation and address a variety of effluents. There are two model-driven algorithms that dictate the dosing of chemicals for consistent and effective performance: AI-driven TSS optimization and model-based optimal pH control. Meat processing wastewater goes into a DAF system.  An on-site embedded PC stores and processes the data from the sensors; the data is then transmitted and further processed into a cloud-based platform. An iOS and Android based app are used for tracking the system performance. A remote monitoring team tracks the system, triaging system alarms to screen out nuisance alarms, identifying root causes, and implementing corrective actions either remotely or through site operator intervention.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Chemicals (caustic soda, acids, coagulant, flocculant) were added by artificial intelligence and model system for TSS and pH control, but amounts were not specified.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow rate is 60 – 100 m3/hr., 12 – 24 hr./day.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Pharmaceutical wastewater from Perrigo plant is sent to the equalization tank after a fine screening , followed by a pH adjustment (if needed) through the flow transfer in the two emergency tanks. The wastewater is then transferred to the cooling system, where the temperature is brought down below 35 degrees Celsius as an effluent preparational step for MBBR unit. Urea and phosphoric acid are used as a dose in the wastewater before entering the MBBR for biological growth. Effluent then passes through two serial MBBR tanks for COD removal where antifoam dosing system is installed to avoid foaming in the reactors. From second MBBR unit, wastewater is sent to the DAF system for secondary solid liquid separation followed by a sludge treatment involving sludge tank and centrifuge.  An odor control system is used to avoid odor emission. The final effluent from the plant is being discharged to public sewage system. Performance data is measured from effluent of equalization tank/influent to MBBR and effluent of DAF during the start-up period (Weeks 1 and 2).
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Urea and Phosphoric acid are being dosed before entering the MBBR for biological growth. An antifoam dosing system is used in MBBR unit to prevent excessive foaming.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The design flow rate of the system is 75 m3/day. Total design HRT of two MBBR unit is 25.6 hours.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Industrial wastewater is sent to the equalization tank after fine screening, followed by pH adjustment (if needed). Nutrients are dosed in the wastewater before entering the MBBR for biological growth. Effluent then passes through three aerobic MBBR stages for organic matter removal where an antifoam dosing system is installed to avoid foaming in the reactors. From the final MBBR stage, wastewater is sent to the pre-fabricated Media Clarifier (MC) for solids separation followed by sludge treatment. The plant's treated wastewater effluent is discharged to public sewage.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: An unknown chemical is added to adjust pH prior to the MBBR. Antifoam and nutrient dosing occurs during the first stage of MBBR unit. Flocculants are dosed into the MBBR effluent just before entering into the Media Clarifier unit.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The design capacity of the industrial stream is 360 m3/d with future expansion to 700 m3/d. The MBBR was designed with a total operative volume of 260 m3 and contained carriers with effective surface area of 650 m2/m3. The MC was designed for solid-liquid separation with surface area of 20.8 m2.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Before upgrades, the engine manufacturing facility consisted of a collector tank, a flow equalization tank, a batch chemical treatment system including two tanks, and an aerobic bioreactor. Process wastewater was continuously conveyed to the collector tank. From there, water is pumped into one of two chemical treatment tanks. In the chemical treatment tank, the wastewater is mixed with chemicals (H2SO4, NaOH and cationic polymer) to break up emulsified oil that was formed on the surface of the water. The pretreated water was then transferred to an aerobic bioreactor for batch treatment. Once the bioreactor is filled with wastewater, air is introduced via a perforated pipe ring at the reactor base until the next batch required treatment. Once the aeration was turned off, the mixed liquor was allowed to settle, and the bioreactor effluent was removed through a nozzle for spray irrigation.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: H2SO4, NaOH, and cationic polymer were added in the batch chemical treatment tanks. Doses were not specified.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: pH in the batch chemical tank was adjusted to an optimum range of 8.5-9.5.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Process wastewater is conveyed to the collector tank where an adjustable drum skimmer is installed for bulk removal of floating oils.  The excess oils from the drum skimmer are transferred to an oil storage tank through an air operated diaphragm pump. Wastewater is then pumped into a new coalescing oil/water separator system for further removal of emulsified oil before reporting to a small effluent tank. Effluent is conveyed from effluent tank to a new ultrafiltration system that is equipped with a tabular membrane ultrafiltration skid. Process wastewater in this unit is continuously recirculated from the process tank through membranes. A portion of the flow passes through the membranes and is conveyed to the upgraded MBR system while the remaining  rejected wastewater is returned to the process tank. The upgraded MBR system has more capacity and includes a new air diffusion system and blowers. In the MBR units, the wastewater is further treated with chemical doses (sodium hydroxide, sulfuric acid, and organosulfide, and phosphoric acid). Finally, MBR effluent is discharged through a nozzle for spray irrigation.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: New chemical storage and feed systems were provided for automated pH control and metals precipitation, including sodium hydroxide, sulfuric acid, and organosulfide. Phosphorus is deficient in the engine plant wastewater as a nutrient for aerobic biological treatment, a phosphoric acid storage and feed system was provided to supplement.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The design membrane flux at the maximum daily hydraulic loading rate of 75 m3/day is 46.5 liters/m2/hour.
MANUFACTURER: Ultrafiltration system: Koch; Membrane bioreactor: GE Water and Process Technologies (now Suez)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: FGD wastewater from overflow storage enters into an evaporative chamber and flows through the heat exchangers where the energy from hot distillate and brine concentrate are used to pre-heat the feed water. The vapor is then captured, compressed, and contained in a reservoir as a liquid distillate.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The project was a commercial 35 gpm system. Total treated water was 2,609,059 gallon over 50-day long pilot study. The recovered volume is 2,152,312 gallon with a high recovery rate (82.5%).
OANDM_COST: Average energy cost of AVARA system at Merom Generating Station is $455.04 per day.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: FGD wastewater originating from coal-fired power plant is pretreated with chemical precipitation to reduce transition metals and dissolved silica. Next, the wastewater passes through the Saltworks' Salt Splitter which is built on two desalination technologies: electrodialysis (ED) and reverse osmosis (RO). The ED step produces both a calcium chloride (CaCl2) and sodium sulfate (Na2SO4) brine. Before the RO step, wastewater is pretreated through either granular media or ultrafiltration. The RO blowdown is sent and mixed with the CaCl2 brine or can be separately concentrated if CaCl2 re-use is preferred. Both brine streams are sent to a downstream processing stage for volume reduction through a small-scale evaporator-crystallizer technology that helps to reduce transition metals and silica loads. The produced sludge is solidified into 85% - 90% pure sodium sulfate and calcium chloride. The RO permeate may be discharged.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium chloride (only for the feed water saturated with calcium sulfate).
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Plant inlet capacity was 1090 m3/day (200 gpm). Pilot plant achieved 90% freshwater recovery.
CAPITAL_COST: Pretreatment and membrane system: $4,113,636, Evaporation-Crystallization System: $2,650,000, Capital: $2.67/m3.
OANDM_COST: Power: $0.065/kWh, Thermal energy: $3/MMBTU, O&M (minus install and labor): $4.44/m3.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Continuously flowing stream of high strength fatty wastewater generated from UDA dairy plant passes through a pre-filtration stage first that removes solids of size 400 micron and larger from the effluent. The wastewater then flows into a 0.05-micron crossflow tubular ceramic microfiltration (CMF) membrane unit, where almost all TSS are removed. Following the filtration treatment in the CMF unit, the treated effluent enters into a RO unit where further removal of TSS, TDS, and remaining COD takes place. The permeate originated from the RO unit is used as potable water on a belt filter spray.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The pore size of CMF membrane is 0.05 micron. For RO unit, seawater thin film composite membrane is used.
MANUFACTURER: Facility plans to switch to new membranes manufactured by Hydranautics.
OANDM_COST: Cost saving in hauling is $800 per day.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Nanofiltration (NF) membrane reject from a copper mine site goes through a first stage desaturation system consisting of lime addition and high rate clarification (i.e., chemical precipitation). The high sulfate wastewater is desaturated, and sulfate is reduced below 1500 mg/L. Addition of seed material during the startup enhances the sludge recirculation. Under a controlled pH, the sulfate was reduced significantly within 30 minutes of reaction.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Lime; seed materials were added during the startup.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: High sulfate gold mining wastewater goes through a first stage high rate clarification process (MULTIFLO) where the effluent is desaturated, and sulfate is reduced below 1800 mg/L. Dosing of lime and anionic polymer during the startup enhances the sludge recirculation. The calcium sulfate sludge produced from this stage is dewatered and disposed of while the first stage effluent is further treated in a second stage high rate clarification system where calcium and aluminum-based salt was added.  As a result, the highly insoluble calcium sulfoaluminate mineral known as ettringite (sulfate species) is precipitated. A portion of the ettringite sludge is recycled back to the second stage after dewatering and a portion of ettringite effluent is post treated for surface discharge or reused while the remainder of the ettringite effluent is treated in third stage aluminum chemical regeneration system where 90% added aluminum is recovered with a hydrochloric acid dose. The effluent from this stage recirculated back to first stage system for ultimate removal of sulfate.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Lime and anionic polymer were dosed to the flocculation tank. Aluminum (recovered) is added in the ettringite precipitation process. Hydrochloric acid was added to the gibbsite recovery reactor.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The process was designed for a flow of 18 gpm (3.8 m3/hr) and 30 minutes retention time in the reactor. The average sludge recycle ratio was 3:1 and the solids settled to 50% sludge volume in 60 minutes. The average underflow solid concentration was 1.2% with a maximum value of 3.3%. Reaction time for ettringite process was 2.5 hours.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Treatment system consists of lime/soda chemical softening to remove the majority of hardness, weak acid cation (WAC) ion exchange to remove residual hardness, two passes of RO to pre-concentrate the brine, followed by forward osmosis and finally evaporation and crystallization. Permeate from the forward osmosis system is recycled to the two-pass RO system. Water is completely consumed by the evaporation/crystallization system.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Addition of lime/soda ash in softening steps.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: The recovery in the minimal liquid discharge system reduces the load on the evaporator by approximately 95% (20.8 m3/hr). The majority of that reduction, 16.5 m3/hr, occurs in the RO membranes, with the remaining 4.3 m3/hr handled by forward osmosis.
OANDM_COST: Reported operating expenses are $24.82 USD/kgal. Power consumption is 10.4 kWhr/m3.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: System consists of partial softening using a tubular microfiltration (TMF) membrane system, followed by a nanofiltration (NF) treatment which is designed to separate out divalent ions (SO4 and residual hardness) from monovalent ions (Na, Cl, etc.). A second pass brackish water RO is used to polish the permeate, and the brine is sent to another, higher pressure rated specialty RO unit before a final evaporation step to recover monovalent salt.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Lime/soda ash may be added during the softening process.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow from NF separation to 2-pass RO is 36 m3/hr, flow from 2-pass RO to high pressure RO is 12 m3/hr, NF separation recovery is up to 80% (in pilot), and 2-pass RO recovery is 67%.

INDUSTRY: Canned and preserved fruits and vegetables processing
TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Wastewater treatment consisted of the following treatment components: equalization tank, coarse screen, fine screen and Cavitation Air Flotation system (CAF), Trickling Filter, MBR, GAC, UV, and RO. The MBR membrane cassettes were filled to the maximum number of modules (28 to 48) and existing modules were replaced to increase surface capacity from 340 sqft to 370 sqft. In terms of MBR aeration, the existing trains and cassettes were converted to LEAPmbr aeration to provide energy and maintenance cost savings. MBR effluent (or permeate) is discharged to a break tank and as part of the multibarrier approach, RO feed is pumped to GAC columns for color and odor removal, followed by UV to eliminate risk of organic fouling, prior to the high-pressure RO feed pumps. RO permeate is discharged to a cistern where it gets distributed to several processes in the Production Facility (i.e., cooling towers, boilers, washing, etc.). The RO concentrate or reject is discharged to sewer.
MEDIA_TYPE: MBR Membrane: ultrafiltration membrane with nominal pore size of 0.04 µm
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: In April 2018, the Sabritas Guadalajara WWTP completed an upgrade to increase treatment capacity to 383,000 gpd (1,450 m3/d) due to additional Production Lines. The plant is operating at 91% of wastewater treatment design capacity (348,700 gpd (1,320 m3/d)) and reusing 77% on average of treated water in their production facility. Table 2 summarizes the operating conditions for 2018 (after expansion).

INDUSTRY: Canned and preserved fruits and vegetables processing
TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: A newly installed AnMBR system is followed by an existing aerobic MBBR system. The AnMBR system is comprised of an anaerobic continuous stirred-tank reactor (An-CSTR) and two membrane tanks equipped with submerged flat sheet membrane units (SMUs). The AnMBR system is designed to fit within the limited space available on-site, and also integrates into the existing downstream MBBR system for aerobic polishing prior to final discharge.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: System is designed for a flow rate of 200000 gpd.
MANUFACTURER: Evoqua is the manufacturer of ADI - AnMBR system

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Pilot system included one feed tank equipped with a mechanical mixer to receive dissolved gas flotation (DGF) effluent. The feed tank volume was 1,000 L.  DGF effluent entered the feed tank by gravity from a skimmer tank, followed by treatment through a single stage MBBR. Performance data was measured at the influent and effluent to the MBBR only.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Study included consistent addition of spent caustic during the Average and Peak Conditions phases. Study also mentioned addition of 20% NH4CI and supplemental COD spike. The spent caustic was metered to the feed tank at a rate of 1.7-2.3 L/hour to achieve a residual alkalinity of 100 mg/L. Water drawn from crude oil storage tank was added occasionally to provide supplemental COD to achieve 275 mg/L COD goal at pilot units. Supplemental TKN (16 mg/L) was added to the pilot influent in the form of NH4Cl solution (54,000 mg/L NH3-N) to mimic full scale characteristics. The NH4Cl solution was pumped from a 1,000 L tote at a rate of 0.5-0.62 L/hr.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Single-stage MBBR: Flow rate = 0.8 m3/hr., HRT = 2.8 hr., Temperature = 26.1 C, Media surface area = 650 m2

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Filtered secondary effluent from the wastewater treatment facility (prior to chlorination) was directed to a demonstration pilot treatment system. The first treatment step is the oxidation/biodegradation process, consisting of ozone and biological activated carbon filtration (BAC). Next, the physical separation process uses ultrafiltration (UF) to separate pathogens. Then, the adsorption process using granulated activated carbon (GAC) to reduce total organic carbon (TOC) and trace pollutants. Finally, the advanced oxidation process includes the addition of hydrogen peroxide and treatment with UV to destroy pathogens and trace pollutants.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Monochloramine is added to prevent biofouling of the UF membranes at a chlorine to ammonia ratio of 4. Hydrogen peroxide is added prior to UV treatment.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Influent flowrate for the pilot treatment system is 20 gpm.
MANUFACTURER: Xylem, Inc. (Oxelia ™ ozone and BAC processes); Calgon (BAC and GAC media); Toray Industries (UF filters); Trojan Technologies (UV)

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Landfill leachate from the Hovgarden landfill in Uppsala, Sweden was collected from the inflow to the on-site water treatment plant and transported to a polypropylene (PP) influent vessel (volume: 300 L). The wastewater was pumped from the influent vessel to a polypropylene column (diameter: 19 cm, water surface height above column bottom: 1.63 m) where foam fractionation took place. In enriching mode, the wastewater entered the column under the water surface at a height of 1.43 m above the column bottom. In stripping mode, the wastewater entered the column above the water surface at a height of 1.83 m above the column bottom. Four brass diffusers (diameter: 18 mm, length: 30 mm) dispersed air at the bottom of the column. A rotameter (0-20 L/min, ZYIA instrument company, FL3-1) controlled the airflow in the column. The inlet air exited the column at the foam exit surface, and effluent from the foam fractionation process exited the column at the column's effluent outlet. The height of the effluent outlet was modified during the experiments to optimize foam collection. The independent variables in the experiments were contact time, air flow, and foam fraction.

 Experiment 6: contact time = 20 min, air flow = 20 L/min, targeted foam fraction = 10%, water flow rate = 2.3 L/min, foam flow rate = 0.23 L/min, effluent flow rate = 2.1 L/min, air ratio = 8.7, operating mode = enriching. 
Experiment 7: contact time = 20 min, air flow = 10 L/min, targeted foam fraction = 10%, water flow rate =  2.3 L/min, foam flow rate = 0.23 L/min, effluent flow rate = 2.1 L/min, air ratio = 4.3, operating mode = enriching.
Experiment 8: contact time = 20 min, air flow = 10 L/min, targeted foam fraction = 20%, water flow rate =  2.3 L/min, foam flow rate = 0.46 L/min, effluent flow rate = 1.8 L/min, air ratio = 4.3, operating mode = enriching. 
Experiment 9: contact time = 20 min, air flow = 10 L/min, targeted foam fraction = 30%, water flow rate =  2.3 L/min, foam flow rate = 0.69 L/min, effluent flow rate = 1.6 L/min, air ratio = 4.3, operating mode = enriching.

Experiment 13: contact time = 15 min, air flow = 13 L/min, targeted foam fraction = 10%, water flow rate =  3.1 L/min, foam flow rate = 0.31 L/min, effluent flow rate = 2.8 L/min, air ratio = 4.3, operating mode = enriching. 
Experiment 16: contact time = 15 min, air flow = 20 L/min, targeted foam fraction = 10%, water flow rate = 3.1 L/min, foam flow rate = 0.31 L/min, effluent flow rate = 2.8 L/min, air ratio = 6.5, operating mode = enriching. 
Experiment 17: contact time = 20 min, air flow = 7.5 L/min, targeted foam fraction = 20%, water flow rate =  2.3 L/min, foam flow rate = 0.46 L/min, effluent flow rate = 1.8 L/min, air ratio = 3.2, operating mode = enriching.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: A leachate collection system discharges into an equalization tank and is combined with surface water in a 1:3 ratio (Note: The leachate is diluted because the flow rate is too low to support plant growth). The wastewater subsequently enters two aeration lagoons operating in parallel for pretreatment, then discharges into a sedimentation tank. Next, the wastewater is pumped into five parallel reed beds, containing an 0.8 m layer of gravel with particle sizes between 30 to 50 mm and planted with Typha angustifolia, Chrysopogon zizanioides, and Cyperus papyrus, with a plant density of 4 plants/m2. The wastewater then flows into five parallel polishing ponds that are planted with water lily, common reed, umbrella sedge, spike rush, and tube sedge. The effluent is then discharged to a water reclamation plant.
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Flow rate of raw leachate (without surface water): 84 m3/day. Equalization tank: hydraulic residence time (HRT) = 0.3 days. Aeration lagoon 1 and 2: surface area (each) = 1,227 m2, HRT = 3.4 days. Sedimentation tank: HRT = 1.3 days. Reed beds 1, 4, and 5: area (each) = 6,000 m2, HRT = 13.65 days. Reed beds 2 and 3: area (each) = 10,000 m2, HRT = 22.75 days. Ponds 1, 2, 3, and 5 each have an HRT of 12 days. Ponds 1, 2, and 5 accept wastewater from reed beds 1, 2, and 5, respectively. Pond 3 accepts wastewater from reed beds 3 and 4. Pond 4 accepts wastewater from ponds 1, 2, 3, and 5, prior to final discharge.

TREATMENT_TECH_DESCRIPTION: Influent raw craft brewery wastewater was first diluted, then entered the GSAnMBR system (granular sludge AnMBR) through an up-flow anaerobic sludge blanket digester, with effluent recirculating between a buffer tank and an external coupled membrane tank. Supernatant from the anaerobic sludge blanket digester overflowed to the buffer tank.
CHEMICAL_ADDITION: Sodium bicarbonate (for pH control)
ADDT_SYSTEM_PARAMETERS: Temperatures were controlled at 37 degrees C, membrane operation flux was set at 10 L/m2/hr. Permeation controlled feeding resulting in a HRT of 38 hours. SRT controlled at 16 days by mixed liquor wasting from the membrane tank.
